picks.headline: Full Game Preview and Score Prediction for Virginia Tech Football vs. SMU
picks.source: Virginia Tech Hokies On SI on MSN
picks.blurb: DALLAS — Virginia Tech football has a towering tilt on its hands today: SMU — the best opponent the Hokies have played all year. Virginia Tech (6-2, 3-2 ACC) became bowl-eligible after capturing a 20-16 victory over Clemson — its first over the Tigers since 2007 — and did not play this past week. SMU (6-2, 4-2 ACC) won six of its first seven games before a 30-27 stumble against Syracuse in the JMA Wireless Dome in Upstate New York. Both teams remain in contention for a spot in the ACC Championship Game and in the top-five unranked squads receiving votes for the AP Top 25, making Friday's contest particularly consequential as the regular season enters its final month. The Mustangs have been nearly untouchable at Gerald J. Ford Stadium, winning all five of their home games this season and each of their 11 ACC home contests since joining the conference in 2024. Virginia Tech, meanwhile, has already captured three road victories against Power Four opponents this season, including breaking its nearly-20-year drought against the Tigers. The Hokies and Mustangs haven't met since 1974, when SMU secured a 28-25 victory. More than five decades later, their first meeting as ACC opponents features two prolific quarterbacks and a pair of potent yet at-times inconsistent defenses. Here's a look at both teams ahead of Friday night's showdown. Virginia Tech's Offense Virginia Tech's offense has found its footing under quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer, who has completed 71.4% of his passes for 2,140 yards, 17 touchdowns, and just two interceptions through eight games. The Penn State transfer has provided a steady presence at center, throwing for at least 250 yards in five contests. However, the Hokies' offensive line has struggled to protect him at times, surrendering six sacks against Clemson. Grunkemeyer's top target has been wide receiver Que'Sean Brown, who leads the team with 685 receiving yards and three touchdowns on 51 receptions. Tight end Luke Reynolds has also emerged as a reliable option, collecting 50 receptions for 493 yards and a team-high six receiving scores. Reynolds caught the game-winning touchdown against Clemson, hauling in a fourth-and-1 pass with 1:44 remaining to put Virginia Tech ahead. On the ground, Jeffrey Overton Jr. has paced the Hokies with 639 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 113 carries, averaging 5.7 yards per carry. Marcellous Hawkins has added 337 yards and five rushing touchdowns, giving Virginia Tech another option out of the backfield. SMU's Offense SMU's offense has been one of the ACC's most productive units this season, averaging 35.3 points and 460-plus yards per game. Quarterback Kevin Jennings has been at the epicenter of that success, completing 73.7% of his passes for 2,414 yards, 21 touchdowns and five interceptions. The fifth-year signal-caller ranks among the nation's leaders in passing efficiency and surpassed 10,000 career passing yards in last week's loss to Syracuse. Jennings threw for 351 yards and two touchdowns against the Orange, but the Mustangs couldn't hold onto their late lead, conceding a game-winning Syracuse touchdown with 17 seconds remaining. Wide receiver Yamir Knight has been one of Jennings' primary targets, leading SMU with 523 receiving yards on 44 receptions and three touchdowns. Knight caught six passes for 80 yards and a touchdown against Syracuse. Running back Kendrick Raphael has provided balance to the Mustangs' passing attack, rushing for 692 yards and nine touchdowns on 135 carries. Raphael is no stranger to Virginia Tech, having scored three touchdowns against the Hokies last season while playing for California. His third touchdown tied the score late in regulation before Virginia Tech prevailed 42-34 in double overtime. Virginia Tech's Defense If Virginia Tech is going to leave Dallas with its seventh victory, its defense must make Jennings uncomfortable. The Hokies lead the nation with 77 tackles for loss and rank sixth nationally in sacks, having brought opposing quarterbacks down 27 times through eight games. Defensive end Aycen Stevens has spearheaded that effort with eight sacks, while defensive tackle Kemari Copeland has contributed four tackles for loss. Virginia Tech's defensive front was particularly disruptive against Clemson, accumulating 13 tackles for loss and four sacks while holding the Tigers to 16 points. In the secondary, cornerback Jaquez White delivered one of the game's defining plays, sacking Clemson's quarterback on the Tigers' final possession on a corner blitz. White finished with a team-high 11 tackles, helping Virginia Tech preserve its four-point advantage. Linebacker Keon Wylie has also been a consistent contributor, recording 41 tackles this season. The Hokies have been especially effective against the run, allowing just 93.4 rushing yards per game. However, their secondary has been less imposing, recording only two interceptions. Against a quarterback of Jennings' caliber, Virginia Tech's ability to generate pressure without exposing its secondary could prove decisive. SMU's Defense SMU's defense presents another difficult challenge for a Virginia Tech offense that has occasionally struggled with pass protection. The Mustangs have registered 22 sacks this season, led by defensive lineman Marques White's 5.5. Linebacker Alexander Kilgore paces the team with 41 tackles. SMU has been particularly effective on third down, allowing opponents to convert just 31 of 115 attempts — a 27% success rate that ranks No. 3 in the nation. The Mustangs have also been difficult to attack through the air, surrendering just 181.8 passing yards per game. Virginia Tech's ability to establish its running game with Overton and Hawkins could be particularly important, especially considering the Hokies were held to just 70 rushing yards against Clemson. Final Thoughts Friday's contest could come down to which team controls the line of scrimmage. Virginia Tech has made a habit of disrupting opposing backfields, but SMU possesses one of the most efficient quarterbacks in college football. Conversely, the Mustangs' pass rush will test an offensive line that has struggled to keep Grunkemeyer upright. The Hokies have already demonstrated their ability to win away from Blacksburg, but Gerald J. Ford Stadium presents a different challenge. SMU has yet to lose at home this season, and the Mustangs will be eager to respond after their disappointing trip to Syracuse. I think SMU will win but that it'll be far from easy. Kickoff is scheduled for 7 p.m. ET on ESPN. Ford Stadium — Dallas, TX Spread: SMU (-6) Over/under: 56.5 All-time series: SMU leads, 2-1 Last meeting: SMU 28, Virginia Tech 25 — September 21, 1974 Current streak: SMU, 2 (1973-74) Setting the scene While No. 1 Miami (FL) and No. 14 Wake Forest are the only ACC teams that reside in the AP Top 25, the conference title race is far from finished. There are five two-loss teams lurking right behind, and two of them clash Friday night in Dallas. It's the first meeting between SMU and Virginia Tech as ACC opponents, however, it's a familiar head coaching matchup: Rhett Lashlee and James Franklin stood on opposite sidelines as recently as 2024 in the College Football Playoff. There's plenty on the line for the bowl eligible opponents. A win would do wonders for remaining in the ACC race, especially for SMU, which can still capture a tiebreaker against Wake Forest. But a third conference loss is essentially an elimination in a 17-team league. Virginia Tech Hokies outlook BLACKSBURG, VIRGINIA - OCTOBER 17: Head coach James Franklin of the Virginia Tech Hokies greets Kaleb Spencer #3 before the game against the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets at Lane Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Blacksburg, Virginia. (Photo by Michael Shroyer/Getty Images) | Getty Images Virginia Tech (6-2, 3-2 ACC) can make another statement on the road after its bye week. The Hokies haven't rattled off seven wins in a regular season since 2019, but that streak could end Friday in year one of the James Franklin era. Virginia Tech is fresh off its biggest win under Franklin, taking down Clemson 20-16 in Death Valley on Oct. 24. Close games have been commonplace for the Hokies this season. Each of their last six contests were decided by 10 points or fewer. Three featured lead changes in the final five minutes, while another ended on a missed field goal attempt that would have resulted in a lead change. The restoration of Virginia Tech football can be attributed to the passing game. Quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer followed Franklin from Penn State and has drastically improved in his junior campaign. Grunkemeyer has connected on an efficient 71.4 percent of attempts — seventh nationally among quarterbacks with 100 attempts — and has delivered 17 touchdowns against two interceptions. Grunkemeyer has eclipsed 300 yards three times and finished seven of his eight starts without throwing a pick. Two receivers have carried a bulk of the load. Wide receiver Que'Sean Brown ranks atop the team with 51 receptions and 685 receiving yards, and he's secured at least five receptions in all eight games. Tight end Luke Reynolds has also been a matchup nightmare for defenses. Reynolds' 50 receptions rank first and his 491 receiving yards ranks third among all FBS tight ends. While a bulk of his production occurred in September, his outing against Clemson was a productive one, snagging two touchdowns on seven receptions. The Hokies aren't as adept in the run game, where they check in at 111th in the FBS with 3.7 yards per carry. They don't incorporate much quarterbaack mobility and primarily rely on the duo of Jeffrey Overton Jr. and Marcellous Hawkins Jr. Overton, a common weapon in the receiving game, showed the extent of his powers in a 209-yard rushing explosion against Boston College. Hawkins has been a steady secondary back, and he's tied for the team lead with five rushing touchdowns. Virginia Tech only surrendered more than 26 points once this season, and that was a Friday night matchup against Pittsburgh. The Hokies' defense has been a positive for the team, tied for 35th in points allowed and ranked 27th in yards allowed per game. Their strength involves limiting the run, where they give up just 93.4 yards per game on a 3.0 average. Sacks heavily factor into that total, and Virginia Tech is the best in the ACC and the sixth-best in the nation at getting to the quarterback, producing 3.4 sacks per game. It's a defensive end led effort. Aycen Stevens ranks first in the conference with 8.0 sacks, while his fellow defensive ends Cortez Harris and Mylachi Williams have 5.0 and 4.5, respectively. The Hokies haven't been as strong on the back end, but they prevent explosive plays well. No team has recorded a 50-yard completion on this defense all season. But what Virginia Tech needs to improve upon is its turnover output. The Hokies forced just five takeaways through eight games, causing the team to enter Friday with a minus-4 in the turnover battle this season. SMU Mustangs outlook DALLAS, TX - OCTOBER 17: Southern Methodist University Mustangs defensive end Marques White (16) rushes the passer during the game between SMU and Virginia on October 17, 2026 at Gerald J. Ford Stadium in Dallas, TX. (Photo by George Walker/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images SMU (6-2, 4-2 ACC) dropped from the rankings after a heartbreaking 30-27 loss at Syracuse last weekend. It was only the Mustangs' fourth conference defeat since joining the ACC, and the third in which they held a lead in the final minute. However, SMU has never lost back-to-back ACC games and owns an 11-0 record in ACC play at home, giving Rhett Lashlee's team the perfect opportunity to bounce back and remain in the conference title race. Slow starts have been the Mustangs' kryptonite. In their last five ACC games, they haven't scored more than 13 points in a half or entered the break with a lead larger than three. However, they've won each of their last five second halves, finishing a plus-68 over that span. SMU's offense is led by Kevin Jennings, who is one of seven passers averaging over 300 yards per game. This season has been a masterclass in efficiency for the senior, who is completing passes at a 73.7 percent clip — the third-highest rate in the country among quarterbacks with 100 attempts. Jennings has also thrown 152 consecutive passes without an interception, with his last misfire coming in the first quarter of a Sept. 26 matchup against Missouri State. The Mustangs' receiver room is as deep as they come, with five different players over the 200-yard threshold. Yamir Knight is the leader with 44 receptions for 523 yards, while Yannick Smith, Jalen Cooper, and Jalen Hale can also pose as explosive threats for an offense that ranks fifth nationally in 50+ yard receptions. Tight ends Randy Pittman Jr. and Theo Melin Öhrstrom are also incorporated into the passing game, and they tie for the team lead with four receptions apiece. Unlike SMU's first ACC defeat at Louisville, last Saturday's loss to Syracuse was largely determined in the trenches. The Mustangs uncharacteristically allowed six sacks, accounting for 43 percent of their season total. Additionally, they struggled to create space for the running backs, which never broke off an explosive gain. Kendrick Raphael has posted three 100-yard games already in ACC play, and he can also do damage out of the backfield as a receiving option. SMU's defense didn't necessarily have a bad outing at Syracuse, limiting the Orange to 5.9 yards per passing attempt and 3.7 yards per rush. But the Mustangs surrendered conversions on all four of Syracuse's fourth down attempts, allowing the Orange to sustain otherwise lost drives. A veteran defensive line full of super seniors is the strength of the unit. SMU ranks 15th nationally with 2.9 sacks per game, and eighth-year senior Marques White leads the way with 5.5 sacks, while the rest of the sacks are quite evenly distributed. The pressure goes hand-in-hand with a strong passing defense, and SMU ranks 28th nationally in fewest passing yards allowed at 182 per game. That is the most improved element of the Mustangs from last year, but losing starting strong safety Tyren Polley for the year could make things difficult down the road. Sael Reyes stepped up last game with 10 tackles in his second start of the season, while Jimmy Wyrick recorded eight from the other safety spot. Lastly, turnovers have been a significant determinant in SMU results this season. The Mustangs lost the turnover battle 5-0 in their two losses, and they're the only bowl eligible team at a minus-5 or worse this season. These 6-2 teams are structured somewhat similarly: strong passing attacks with tight end utilization, dominant defensive fronts that repeatedly get to the quarterback, and solid defenses hampered by poor turnover margins. Short weeks oftentimes favor the home team, and SMU remains perfect against ACC opponents at Gerald J. Ford Stadium. Given SMU's discrepancy between first and second half performance, Virginia Tech may enter halftime with the lead, but the Mustangs ultimately rally behind Kevin Jennings in the fourth quarter to secure a one-score win on The Hilltop. Prediction: SMU 30, Virginia Tech 24

Ahead of the clash, here's our staff's predictions as to what will unfold tonight in the Lone Star State. JACKSON CAUDELL: While it will still be a long shot even if they find a way to win, the Hokies' ACC hopes are on the line tomorrow night at SMU. The Mustangs are also battling for their ACC title hopes, and that makes this a fascinating matchup. This is a chance for James Franklin to land another win against one of the better programs in the conference, and I think they have the offense to take advantage of a suspect SMU defense. If the Hokies can get after Kevin Jennings and force a few turnovers, I think they are able to do that and score a big win. Final score prediction: Virginia Tech 31, SMU 27 JAMES DUNCAN: Syracuse left a blueprint last Saturday, beating SMU 30-27 on a touchdown with 17 seconds left. Virginia Tech is built to follow it. Nobody has beaten the Hokies by more than five points this season, and they come in with 13 days of rest to SMU's six. Ethan Grunkemeyer has thrown 17 touchdowns and two interceptions, and both picks came in one night against Pitt. He won't hand Kevin Jennings free possessions, which puts the game on Brent Pry's defense. That group made 13 tackles for loss at Clemson, and it won't need half that many Friday if it gets off the field on third down. Friday won't be a rout, but I think the Hokies give the Mustangs their first home loss in the ACC. Final score prediction: Virginia Tech 30, SMU 28 THOMAS HUGHES: Let's get this out of the way: SMU has never lost an ACC game at home. Its strongest wins at Gerald J. Ford Stadium this season, however, came against Virginia and California - two squads with a combined 7-11 (4-8 ACC) record. The Hokies should be well-equipped to contend with the Mustangs, though SMU signal-caller Kevin Jennings may present Tech with its toughest test of the season yet. Virginia Tech quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer has been stellar this campaign, throwing 17 touchdowns to just two interceptions, and while I expect another strong performance from him, I think SMU narrowly edges Virginia Tech in Dallas tonight. Final score prediction: SMU 31, Virginia Tech 28 KADEN REINHARD: I think this game will be defined by one word over the 60 minutes of action: Intensity. Several factors will fuel that fire: Friday night lights, the Mustangs coming off the Syracuse loss and Tech finding itself back in the receiving-votes category of the AP Top 25. But most importantly, I see both offenses locking into a close-knit battle, as both sides can mend their attacks with a healthy mix of the ground and air attack. Ultimately, I think the Hokies' defense can handle the contest by not allowing SMU quarterback Kevin Jennings to extend many plays outside the pocket, which has been a struggle for the Hokies in recent years. picks.blurb: Three Bold Predictions for Virginia Tech vs. SMU - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NFL news, live updates Misiorowski, Schlittler win Cy Youngs NFL midseason awards Rex Ryan arrested Skubal suitors emerge Three Bold Predictions for Virginia Tech vs. SMU Virginia Tech Hokies tight end Luke Reynolds (85) scores near Clemson safety Jerome Carter III (6) during the second quarter at Memorial Stadium Saturday, October 24, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect James Duncan · Virginia Tech Hokies On SI Fri, November 6, 2026 at 2:37 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Seventeen seconds remained in the JMA Wireless Dome on Saturday, when Syracuse quarterback Steve Angeli found tight end Noah Meyers alone on the left side of the end zone. Meyers had never scored for the Orange before that catch. The touchdown beat SMU 30-27 and knocked the Mustangs out of the AP Top 25. Virginia Tech should have that clip on a loop. The Hokies (6-2, 3-2 ACC) visit SMU (6-2, 4-2) at 7 p.m. ET Friday on ESPN. The Mustangs are 5-0 at Gerald J. Ford Stadium this season and 6.5-point favorites. Their defense holds up better against the pass than the run, and its injuries are stacked in the middle of the field. Two of my predictions start there. The third starts with what Syracuse did to Kevin Jennings. 1. Luke Reynolds has his best game since September SMU doesn't give much away through the air. Opponents complete 62.6% of their passes and average 6.0 yards per attempt. The one real hole is at safety. Sophomore Tyren Polley Jr., third on the team with 34 tackles, tore a pectoral muscle in October and is out for the season. SMU has played two games without him: a 59-20 win over Cal and the loss at Syracuse. Help could be coming. Ahmaad Moses, a first-team All-ACC safety in 2025, is questionable after missing the whole season while SMU works on his eligibility. The junior tight end has 50 catches for 493 yards and six touchdowns, and his 50 catches lead all FBS tight ends. The last three games have been quieter: 13 catches for 120 yards since Pitt. Two of those 13 went for touchdowns at Clemson, including the go-ahead score in the fourth quarter. Friday, he clears 100 receiving yards for the third time this season and finds the end zone again. 2. Jeffrey Overton Jr. snaps his 100-yard drought Overton last reached 100 yards on Sept. 26, when he ran for 209 at Boston College, the sixth-highest single-game total in Virginia Tech history. He has 230 yards in four games since and averaged 2.6 yards per carry at Clemson. The sophomore still leads the Hokies with 639 yards on 113 carries. Two things change Friday. The first is the offensive line. "We're going to get some guys back, which is helpful, especially on the offensive line," coach James Franklin said Monday. Guard/tackle Montavious Cunningham and guard Brody Meadows are expected to play. Left tackle Justin Terry is still out. The second is the defense across from him. SMU allows 125.9 rushing yards per game and 3.8 yards per carry. Those numbers flatter the Mustangs. College football counts sacks as rushing plays, and SMU has 23 sacks for 148 yards. Pull them out, and opponents are averaging 4.8 yards per designed run. Those 23 sacks matter for Virginia Tech in another way. Ethan Grunkemeyer has been sacked 23 times himself. A run game that works keeps the Hokies on schedule and gives SMU's rushers something else to think about. Overton gets his third 100-yard game of the season. 3. Virginia Tech sacks Kevin Jennings at least four times Before Halloween, SMU hadn't allowed more than two sacks in a game this season. Syracuse got six. Look at who was playing on the left side. True freshman Drew Evers moved over from right tackle to start at left tackle, and fellow true freshman Sam Utu made his first career start beside him at left guard. It was only the second college game of his career. SMU could get some help back. Guard Alex Woods, a starter, missed Syracuse, and tackle Andrew Chamblee, who has started at both tackle spots, hasn't played since Oct. 17. Neither is on Thursday's availability report. Watch the first series to see who lines up on the left. Either way, Virginia Tech has the rushers to test it. The Hokies average 3.4 sacks per game, sixth in FBS, and three players have more than four: Aycen Stevens with eight, Cortez Harris with five and Mylachi Williams with 4.5. Defensive tackle Kemari Copeland said this week the plan is to "cage" Jennings and take away his scrambles to the right. Friday, the Hokies get to Jennings at least four times. Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The annual Holy War has been declared between Utah and BYU. Just about everything is on the line. That includes serious College Football Playoff consideration. Utah is undefeated and has a straight line to the Big 12 championship. BYU has a big win over Notre Dame, but also a loss to unranked UCF that complicates its resume. What happens here will affect the top of the playoff committee's rankings this week. Here are five matchups in the game we're keeping a close eye on. 1. BYU's Biggest Danger BYU's biggest vulnerability remains its struggling rushing attack. The Cougars managed just 47 rushing yards against Arizona State, averaging 1.6 yards per carry. Injuries along the offensive line and uncertainty surrounding running back LJ Martin's availability only add to the concern. Utah ranks 22nd nationally in rushing defense, allowing just 101.4 yards per game. If the Utes shut down BYU's ground game, quarterback Bear Bachmeier could face constant pressure in obvious passing situations. If so, that could make BYU's offense predictable and allow Utah's defense to dictate the game. 2. Utah's Biggest Danger Dec 31, 2025; Las Vegas, NV, USA; Utah Utes quarterback Devon Dampier (4) throws the ball against the Nebraska Cornhuskers in the second half during the SRS Distribution Las Vegas Bowl at Allegiant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Utah's dual-threat quarterback Devon Dampier is central to its offensive success. However, BYU's defensive front could present problems if it consistently wins its assignments and limits Dampier's ability to escape the pocket. If BYU forces Utah into third-and-long situations and eliminates explosive running plays, the Utes could struggle to maintain their offensive rhythm. 3. The Fast Start Factor Utah has been outstanding in opening quarters, outscoring opponents 89-6 in the first quarter this season. If the Utes jump ahead early, BYU could be forced to abandon its preferred offensive approach. Conversely, an early BYU lead could put pressure on an undefeated Utah team playing in a rivalry game it hasn't won since 2019. More: Predicting Big 12 football scores for Week 10's biggest games 4. Special Teams and Turnovers BYU has a significant advantage in special-teams efficiency, ranking seventh nationally in SP+ compared with Utah's 77th. Field position could become critical. Turnovers could also swing the game. Utah cannot afford to give BYU short fields, particularly in a potentially tight fourth quarter. 5. The Bottom Line BYU's nightmare is getting physically dominated up front. Utah's nightmare is allowing BYU to turn the game into a defensive, turnover-filled rivalry battle. Both teams have clear paths to making Saturday uncomfortable for the other. The Big Lead prediction: Utah 24, BYU 21

The most anticipated game in the history of the BYU-Utah rivalry. The stakes couldn't be higher for no. 9 BYU . The Cougars used their mulligan in a road loss at UCF. They would lose control of their own destiny if they don't beat Utah. On the other hand, a win over Utah could propel BYU into the top five and in the drivers seat for a spot in the CFP. To win this game, BYU needs to keep the game close in the first quarter. The Utes have outscored their opponents by more than 70 points and have not allowed a touchdown in the first quarter. Utah has scored touchdowns on its opening drive in seven out of eight games. Utah offensive coordinator Kevin McGiven has been brilliant with his opening scripted drives. Given the emotions going into this game, the unusual kickoff time, and Utah's track record of strong starts, BYU needs to weather the early storm at Rice Eccles Stadium. If BYU can settle in and adjust to Utah's unique offense, the Cougars will have a great chance to pull off the upset. BYU is expected to get LJ Martin back in the lineup for the first time since early October against TCU. How effective and how healthy Martin will be remains to be seen. On offense, Bear Bachmeier will have to carry another heavy load. Bachmeier will have chances to throw from clean pockets against a Utah defense that will give up explosive plays through the air. Bachmeier and his wide receivers, particularly deep threat Legend Glasker, need to have a big game. BYU is the best defense Utah will have faced by a wide margin. Even though the BYU defense has struggled to bring ball-carriers to the ground, we like their chances to keep the Utah offense somewhat in check. picks.blurb: my favs Access and manage your favorites here DISMISS Scores SPORTS & TEAMS PERSONALITIES POPULAR SEARCHES College Football Add FOX Sports on Google 2026 College Football Week 10 Expert Picks: BYU-Utah Set For All-Time Holy War Published Nov. 5, 2026 3:25 p.m. ET share facebook x reddit link Geoff Schwartz FOX Sports Betting Analyst This weekend, we've got the Holy War and just another SEC battle. Here is how I'm wagering college football Week 10. This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX Sports may be compensated. Read more about Sports Betting on FOX Sports . No. 9 BYU @ No. 3 Utah This Holy War might be the holiest of them all: Utah hosting bitter rival BYU, with the winner in the driver's seat for a Playoff spot. It’s the first time both teams have been ranked in the top 10 for this matchup, and I can’t wait to start the day with this one. I think BYU might win outright. It has been tested with its win over Notre Dame just a few weeks ago. Yes, it lost to UCF the following week in a typical trap game — big home win followed by a road conference game. Otherwise, the Cougars have handled business, even though the scores don’t seem that impressive. BYU is built on defense. It is 13th in yards per play and it limits explosives. It does not rush the passer all that well, but against Utah’s rushing attack, that might not be needed. BYU’s defense already faced a high-powered offense in the Irish and limited it to a negative EPA rushing day. Utah’s offensive production slowly ticked down when conference play started, but it did bounce back last week against a poor Cincinnati defense. Utah has played one defense in the same realm as BYU and that was Houston. Utah struggled to score, only putting up 21 points with seven of those happening super late after forcing a Houston turnover. Will the BYU offense find a groove against Utah? (Getty Images) It’s fair to also believe BYU’s offense might struggle in this game. However, it appears the Cougars are getting stud running back LJ Martin back, and they are much better when Martin is on the field. He’s averaging almost eight yards a carry with 20% of his rushes going for 10+ yards. Utah’s defense is the typical physical front against the run, but BYU is the best offense the Utes have faced all season. Utah’s pass rush concerns me. It is 80th in pressure rate and unless it blitzes, it isn't able to get to the quarterback. Seems less than ideal against BYU quarterback Bear Bachmeier. I see these teams as even. They are both defensively based with an offense that wants to run the ball. That’s too many points in a game like this. I’ll take BYU to cover. Schwartz's Pick: BYU -4.5 No. 5 Alabama @ No. 14 LSU In the newly-released CFP rankings, Alabama is fifth and is an underdog at LSU by almost a touchdown. I do lean towards LSU at -6, but that number feels big. Instead, I’m going to fade Alabama’s offense in this game. Alabama is facing its fourth straight difficult defense, and in the first three games, we’ve seen the offensive efficiency drop. Quarterback Keelon Russell is nearing the end of his first season as a starting quarterback, and he’s been mostly excellent for his age. However, he has struggled the last three weeks outside the end of the Texas A&M game. Against Georgia, Tennessee and A&M, he completed only 60% of passes with just four passing touchdowns and three interceptions. Alabama’s beat-up offensive line has allowed 11 sacks in the three previous games. Now, the Tide play an LSU defense that’s first in sacks per pressure and 11th in pressure rate. The Bama offensive line and Russell were noticeably affected by the environment in Tennessee, and now they are at LSU. I feel most comfortable with Alabama not scoring much in this game. Klatt's Week 10 Picks Updated Nov. 5, 2026 11:36 a.m. ET share facebook x reddit link The long-awaited, top-25-filled Week 10 of the college football season is finally here. Everything from College Football Playoff implications to potential conference championship matchups are in play this Saturday. Starting at 12 p.m. ET, No. 9 BYU heads to No. 3 Utah for the annual Holy War rivalry matchup, with instant CFP and Big 12 title impact. The day ends with No. 1 Miami at No. 11 Notre Dame in a rematch of the game that arguably kept the Fighting Irish out of last year's CFP. Especially after Tuesday's first CFP rankings of the season — which FOX Sports' Joel Klatt raised concerns about — this weekend's slate will make a heavy impact on the postseason playoff picture. Here at Klatt's Week 10 picks and previews, from the latest episode of "The Joel Klatt Show": No. 1 Miami (Fla.) vs. No. 11 Notre Dame (Photo by Samuel Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Spread: Notre Dame -5.5 Moneyline: Notre Dame -238, Miami +195 Klatt's thoughts: " Notre Dame, you got to win … The committee really put Notre Dame behind the eight ball. They're backed into a corner. So, don't we all expect to get Notre Dame's best? I mean, we have to … Now, Miami has taken care of business. Notre Dame did not. They got beat by BYU. Yes, there was a second left. They didn't get that snap, and so here they are with their backs against the wall. "Let's take a look at this game from just like: what's the strongest thing? What's the weakest thing that any of these teams do? Well, if you're looking at the weakest thing, I always look at that, because in a matchup game typically the weakest link of the teams is what's going to end up getting you beat, and the weakest thing that anybody does in this game is Miami's defense, and we've seen that over the last, what, three weeks and three games. Two of the last three games, they've given up 35 points to Florida State and UNC. So it's not a great defense. It is not nearly the defensive front that they had a year ago. Their secondary is not great. "So they've got to find a way to limit CJ Carr, who I think is one of the better quarterbacks that we have in the country. What's the strongest part of this game? It's Miami's offense. It's interesting. They've got the strongest part. They've got the weakest part. Their ceiling with their offense is outstanding. I think it's the best thing anybody does in college football. Darian Mensah film is fantastic. I love watching it. "I'm going to go to Notre Dame. I think that they have to win, and they will win because, again, the committee is doing Miami no favors here … Notre Dame 30-27. Miami, I'll take the 5.5." Klatt's straight-up pick: Notre Dame Klatt's pick against the spread: Miami +5.5 No. 9 BYU vs. No. 3 Utah (Photo by Bryan Byerly/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) Spread: Utah -4.5 Moneyline: Utah -198, BYU +164 Klatt's thoughts: "BYU at Utah. Holy War. 4.5 is the spread here. Utah is favored. Utah has lost three straight in this series, including a home game. BYU has not looked great since the Notre Dame game. I think we would all agree with that. Utah has been a team that has been very impressive, which is largely why they're ranked No. 3 in the country right now. Because even though they've played something north of a wet paper bag, the committee decided that they were the third-ranked team in the country. That was a shot. It wasn't meant to be a shot. Because I love Utah. You know I love you, Utah. Death, taxes, Utah football. They roared back against Houston after being down 10-0 at around halftime. They destroyed Cincinnati. They're a difficult team to beat on the road when they're in their home stadium. Devon Dampier and Wayshawn Parker are dynamic. The one concern I would have for Devon Dampier is the turnovers. "You can't do that in this game, not in this game. And, in particular, with an aggressive BYU defense … They're going to have to run the football, play quality defense, and use the energy of that stadium to their benefit. LJ Martin for BYU could be back. I don't know how effective he will be, but they need that because they have not been able to run the football very well over the last couple of weeks. Speaking of BYU, both have good defenses. Although, gosh, you know I love Kalani Sitake. I think Kalani Sitake is fantastic, but his defense the last couple of weeks hasn't been like BYU standard. I personally believe this Utah team has something to prove. Almost like their coach retired and then took another job somewhere else. It's like it resembles that. I don't know if that was the case or not, but that's what it looks like. And Morgan Scalley has been there for a long time, and he understands the culture of Utah. And I think this team is playing with an edge. " Utah 27, BYU 20. Utah covers the 4.5." Klatt's straight-up pick: Utah Klatt's pick against the spread: Utah -4.5 No. 2 Georgia vs. No. 10 Ole Miss (Photo by Roger Wimmer/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) Spread: Georgia -3.5 Moneyline: Georgia -175, Ole Miss +145 Klatt's thoughts: "Georgia at Ole Miss. This one could be a great game. I really think it could be. Georgia is favored by 3.5. Rematch to that quarterfinal from a year ago. Ole Miss won that one. Trinidad Chambliss was outstanding in that ball game, and I'm sure Kirby Smart has had nightmares about Trinidad Chambliss ever since then. And now he's got to go to Oxford, and he's got to play Trinidad Chambliss where Trinidad Chambliss has never lost a start. Ole Miss is not going to have Kewan Lacy, he's likely out in this game. Trinidad Chambliss is a guy that I love. You guys, I know I've loved him ever since the beginning of the year, and now he gets to face Kirby Smart. And this team is the best road team that we have in the country over the last several years. Why? Because they're consistent. Why? Because they run the football. Because they play good defense. These are the things that travel. These are the things that allow you to have success on the road. I do think it's going to be a close game. I don't think Georgia is going to be able to separate in this game, but they're too consistent. They're too consistent. "If Georgia can hold Ole Miss to field goals, I think that's where the game is won or lost. If it's high scoring, I favor Ole Miss because Trinidad runs wild. If it's lower scoring and in the 20s, then I favor Georgia because it's a slug fest, and you're kicking field goals, and it's third down and it's situations. What do I think it's going to be? More of a slug fest. "I'm going to take Georgia 28-24 . They cover the 3.5 on the road." Klatt's straight-up pick: Georgia Klatt's pick against the spread: Georgia -3.5 No. 23 Oregon vs. No. 12 Ohio State (Photo by Melinda Meijer/ISI Photos/Getty Images) Spread: Ohio State -7.5 Moneyline: Ohio State -305, Oregon +245 Klatt's thoughts: " Oregon at Ohio State . Ohio State favored by 7.5. Interesting. So Vegas likes Ohio State a lot more than the committee does. By the way, Oregon has a path to the Big Ten championship game. I know we haven't talked about that a lot on this program, but I know other programs have mentioned it. Yes, that's absolutely the case. And if I were Oregon, I would smell the blood in the water a little bit. "This is not the same Ohio State that came into Eugene a couple of years ago and would eventually win the national championship. And it is certainly not the same Ohio State that you saw in the Rose Bowl, and that kind of, you know, blew the hinges off in that game. I don't know what we're going to get. Luke Fahey is going to start at QB again. How long is the leash for Luke Fahey? Not sure. I don't think he played very well … I thought the ball went to the wrong spot a few times. He overthrew some open wide receivers, and they didn't get the ball to Jeremiah Smith. "Jay Johnson is [Oregon's] new offensive coordinator after they fired Drew Mehringer after that Illinois game, and they looked a lot better in the second half against Northwestern. This is a very different defense than they're going to face. I think this is a much better secondary, and I would think that Matt Patricia of Ohio State is going to find a way to put pressure on Dylan Raiola. He does not deal with pressure well. It's like Ohio State's backed into a corner … You just get all of Ohio State, and if you get all of Ohio State, that means that you get all of Jeremiah Smith , and they're going to be taking shots, and they're going to be more aggressive even with a young quarterback, because you got nothing to lose. "I'm going to say Ohio State wins this game. They have to. They win it 30-20 . They cover the 7.5." Klatt's straight-up pick: Ohio State Klatt's pick against the spread: Ohio State -7.5 No. 5 Alabama vs. No. 14 LSU (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Spread: LSU -5.5 Moneyline: LSU -225, Alabama +185 Klatt's thoughts: " Alabama at LSU , always a great game. LSU is favored by 5.5 over the committee's fifth-ranked team. You mean Vegas doesn't agree with the committee either? No, they don't. No one does. Literally, no one. Not even Bama fans … Bad matchup for Alabama in this one. I think it's a terrible matchup for Alabama. Let me tell you why, because if Kalen DeBoer gets into a big game, typically they throw the football a lot and they don't run it very well. And when that happens, they have to protect their quarterback. And if they can't protect their quarterback, they don't win. And LSU is a terrific pass rushing team. Terrific, second in the country in sacks. Meanwhile, you would think that Alabama on the offensive line would do a good job protecting their quarterback. Not the case. We saw pressure against Tennessee, pressure against Georgia, and LSU might be better in the pass rush than both of those teams. Bad matchup. I don't think they're going to be able to run the football. "Speaking of Alabama … They beat Mississippi State, who was undefeated at the time. Each of the last two times that they played LSU in Death Valley, Alabama has been held under 70 yards rushing, and that's even with better Alabama teams and teams that are more willing to run the football. So again, all of this leads to: Do I think LSU can at least get out of their own way offensively, not turn the football over and score some points? The answer is yes. Sam Leavitt is playing better. the year takes place this Saturday at Rice-Eccles Stadium between #9 BYU (7-1) and #3 Utah (8-0). It’s the Holy War! Both teams sit atop the Big 12, and the winner of this game is likely in the Big 12 Championship, whereas the loser can’t afford another loss to make the conference title game. Utah is enjoying its highest ranking in program history, and depending on what happens this weekend, the Utes could end up No. 1. Devon Dampier has led an electric offense averaging 38.9 points per game (11th) in their first year without Kyle Whittingham and with Morgan Scalley at the helm; but the defense has been incredible! The Utes have been a tank from the start. Utah averages 10.3 first-quarter points per game (T-4th) and allows 0.9 (1st) defensively. Utah has gassed up opponents early and carried a lead late; that’s been their M.O. Utah is on the nation’s longest winning streak, 14 games, after thrashing Cincinnati 49-25. The last loss came against BYU 24-21 last season. Utah can get revenge and, in the same breath, claim control of their destiny and the Big 12. If BYU loses to Utah, the Cougars’ college football hopes will rely on winning the Big 12 Championship. With a loss to UCF, BYU put their season on thin ice as Utah, BYU, and Texas Tech battle for the top two spots. BYU had a strong first half against Arizona State last week, leading 17-3 at the break, but was outscored 17-10 in the second half. BYU could get a boost this week with star running back and 2025 Big 12 Offensive Player of the Year LJ Martin returning. Martin has missed the last four games and put a lot of the offensive pressure on Bear Bachmeier . While reports say Martin won’t be 100 percent if he plays, at least he could be a decoy that sets up Bachmeier in RPO or the downfield pass game. Let’s dive into the schools on both sides of the ball, look at a few key players, and see where the numbers take us. Utah scored a ridiculous 42 points in the first half and led 42-6 at the half. The Utes scored on all four of their offensive drives in the first half, and the defense recorded a pick-six and fumble return for a touchdown. The Utes didn’t score on the first four drives of the second half, but it didn’t make much of a difference; the damage was already done to the Bearcats. Utah enters hot and ready for a shootout at 10 AM their time! Utah Player to Watch on Offense: QB Devon Dampier For the third time in the last four games, Devon Dampier threw three touchdown passes and 200-plus yards in seven straight. Dampier’s been on fire, and even when he’s not slinging touchdowns, he’s running for them. Dampier had 150 rushing yards and two touchdowns against Houston, then turned around and threw for three scores on Cincinnati. In the last four games, Dampier has 12 total touchdowns to one interception and averaged 309.5 total yards in that span, with Utah scoring 34.5 points per game. The Utes have been a tank, and if they win this game, Dampier can jump into the top five odds for the Heisman. The Utah Utes Defense: Utah’s defense has been one of my favorite units to watch this season. They fly around and lay the boom on opponents from the opening drive. Utah allowed over 200 yards in the first half, but Cincinnati couldn’t convert in the red zone, nor on the money downs. Cincinnati went 3-of-13 on third and fourth downs and only managed a 24:30 time of possession. It was a dominant performance from Utah, and in the first quarter, they’ve been the best team all season. Utah’s defense has allowed six total first-quarter points all season and a 0.9 first-quarter points-per-game average, which leads the country. Getting off to a quick start seems impossible for opponents this season; let’s see what BYU can do. Utah Player to Watch on Defense: DB Jackson Bennee In Utah’s biggest game of the season, Jackson Bennee posted a season-high eight tackles, had a sack, forced and recovered a fumble against Houston, then recorded four tackles against Cincinnati the following week. Bennee ranks third on the Utes with 36 tackles, third in pass deflections (4), and tied for the team lead in interceptions (2). Bennee led the team in picks last year (4) and was second in tackles (63), so he’s off to another strong season. A win at Utah would help his case in a weekend where the Heisman Trophy race will have major chaos. BYU ranks 42th in passing grades per PFF and Utah is 47th in coverage grades, so that will be the biggest battle, outside of these massive offensive lines clashing in the trenches. Martin was hurt against TCU, and the game prior, he posted a season-high 176 rushing yards and three touchdowns against Colorado State. Whether he is or is not 100 percent, Martin can be utilized in the red zone and short-yardage situations, plus the senior would be a great decoy for play-action early. The BYU Cougars Defense: BYU’s defense had one of its best first-half showings of the season against Arizona State. The Cougars held the Sun Devils to 107 yards and three points in the first half, but the second half was a different story. BYU gave up two straight touchdown drives of 12 and 13 plays for 81 and 39 yards. After that, a punt and field goal pulled the game within seven. BYU played the second half very conservatively in order to hold onto the win and come out healthy. BYU had six sacks, 8 TFL, and forced two fumbles. Uluave led Cal last year with 97 tackles, was second in sacks (3.5), and fourth in pass deflections (4). Uluave has been a four-year starter in college and is an Utah native (South Jordan, UT). This will be a memorable game for Uluave; playing in his first and only Holy War. away.blurb: Martin was, indeed, available against the Utes, though he was barely seen in the second half and recorded just eight touches for 24 yards. "He's not even close [to 100%]. ... He gave us everything he had when he could go and did some good things, and hopefully we can get more out of him each week. But he's still got a ways to go." Heading into Week 10, there was uncertainty about whether or not the BYU Cougars would be getting star running back LJ Martin back on the field for their matchup with the Utah Utes . He had suffered an ankle injury in early October against TCU, sidelining him for the next four games. After practice on Wednesday, BYU offensive coordinator Aaron Roderick offered up an update on Martin's status. Part of the reason that the Cougars needed Martin's presence against the Utes was because of other injuries at the running back position. While Sione Moa returned a couple weeks ago after suffering an injury in the season-opener, Preston Rex, entrusted with the RB1 reps in BYU's big win over Notre Dame, wasn't on the field against Utah with an injury, his second straight game missed. Roderick also spoke on Rex's status, saying that he believes Rex will be good to go come Saturday against the Baylor Bears. With just three weeks remaining in the regular season, the BYU running back room remains an uncertain spot on the roster. But if Martin and Rex can regain full strength soon, the Cougars will be in a good spot heading into what they hope is an appearance in the College Football Playoff in mid December. How he feels pre-game will determine extent of his role." Even a limited Martin is likely a boost for BYU's offense as a whole. He's talented enough to serve as both a playmaker and even a useful decoy. BYU has figured out how to play with Martin — including in a win over Notre Dame, although they then lost the next week to UCF — but the Cougars would much rather take the field with Martin in uniform to try and win the Holy War. home.headline: BYU’s LJ Martin Gets Major Injury Update From ESPN Before Utah
home.blurb: Martin is a star running back who has been out for about a month due to injury. Earlier this week, the comments coming from BYU made it seem like Martin may miss out even on the Utah game. “Star running back LJ Martin of No. 9 BYU is trending toward dressing and being available to play in the Cougars' showdown against No. 3 Utah in Salt Lake City, sources told ESPN's Pete Thamel on Wednesday.” It's a fascinating contrast, because the Big 12's official availability report lists Martin as doubtful. “Martin is officially doubtful for the game, per the initial Big 12 availability report released Wednesday night,” ESPN writes, “but sources said the reigning conference Offensive Player of the Year is trending toward playing Saturday and having some impact on the game, although he's not expected to be 100% if he does go.” It's notable that Martin isn't expected to be 100% even if he plays, but BYU would love to have any version of Martin out there on the field. It all will depend on what happens Saturday as to whether Martin's absence, and return, have had the impact hoped for with BYU. BYU's LJ Martin Gets Major Injury Update From ESPN Before Utah The BYU Cougars can't afford to lose on Saturday against their in-state rival Utah Utes. It's called the Holy War for a reason, but it's also a massive matchup with College Football Playoff implications. If BYU wins, they'll control their own CFP destiny the rest of the way. If the Cougars lose, they may need a lot of help to eventually sneak into the back end of the Playoff field. With all that on the line, BYU would love to have its best players on the field, and the list of question marks begins with LJ Martin. But the latest news is a lot better. The latest report came from ESPN on Wednesday night: The ESPN article adds that “a final decision will be made later in the week.” He sustained a lower-body injury in a win over TCU on Oct. 3 and hasn't played since. BYU beat Notre Dame without Martin, but then they lost in double overtime to UCF in what could prove to be a costly defeat. Martin ran for 1,305 yards last season on 5.5 yards per carry with 12 touchdowns, and he also caught 36 passes for 255 yards. This season, he has 44 runs for 344 yards with three TDs along with five catches for 41 yards. In the four games he has missed, it has been mostly Sione Moa and Preston Rex filling in for Martin. They've done a solid job, but neither is BYU's RB1, who they'll be hoping can get back on the field on Saturday. Billy Heyen Billy Heyen is a Heavy contributor with focus on the NFL and MLB. As of Thursday's availability report, Martin was upgraded to questionable. According to ESPN's Pete Thamel, Martin is trending in the right direction to be available on Saturday. "Martin practiced the last three days for BYU. He’s on track to dress and attempt to play on Saturday," Thamel wrote . "He’ll likely be limited, but he’s determined to impact the game. Another eventuality could be only if he’s needed. Perhaps in the goal line or primarily first downs. Even if Martin is only used sparingly, it’s a win for the BYU Cougars to have that option. BYU’s ability to beat a top program in Notre Dame without the services of Martin should remain an optimistic factor for fans. If the Cougars can add in Martin, even if it's strategic, and he’s limited, the outlook for BYU in this game is brighter than it would be without him. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings Two former Big 12 foes are set to clash for the first time as members of the SEC on Saturday Getty Images No. 7 Texas and No. 18 Missouri will square off as SEC foes for the first time on Saturday in a clash between two-loss teams seeking traction in the College Football Playoff picture. The Tigers (6-2, 3-2 SEC) have already blown out league foes Florida and Texas A&M at home this season and are 13-3 at Faurot Field against league opposition since 2023. Taking on Texas (6-2, 3-2) represents an uptick in competition, but the Tigers shouldn't be lacking confidence. Florida was No. 8 in the AP poll when it arrived at Mizzou on Oct. 3. It left with a 45-17 loss that legitimized Missouri and showed its full potential. Since then, we've also seen Missouri's floor, which was found in a 31-3 loss at Ole Miss on Oct. 17. But after a bye week and a 34-10 "get right" win over Arkansas in Week 9, the Tigers appear to be back on track. The Longhorns are entering off wins over Ole Miss and Mississippi State , but their vaunted offense is still falling short of expectations. Is this the point when everything will start to click for quarterback Arch Manning ? If a Texas team that spent four weeks at No. 1 earlier this season is going to meet expectations, a breakthrough needs to come soon. Where to watch Texas vs. Missouri live Date : Saturday, Nov. 7 | Time : 12 p.m. ET Location : Faurot Field -- Columbia, Missouri TV: ESPN | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Texas vs. Missouri: Need to know Injuries mount for Texas: Injuries are adding up for the Longhorns, who enter this matchup with star receivers Ryan Wingo and Cam Coleman listed as questionable. Wingo is dealing with a quad injury while Coleman is working through a shoulder issue. Both have appeared in all eight games for Texas up to this point while combining to catch 11 of Arch Manning's 15 touchdown passes. Star edge rusher Collin Simmons is also questionable after missing Texas' past two games because of an ankle injury. That's a lot of star power in the "questionable" category for Texas. By contrast, Missouri's injury report is nearly clean. Welcome back, Ahmad: Missouri running back Ahmad Hardy made his 2026 debut last week, carrying the football twice in the Tigers' win over Arkansas. The 2025 All-American has been on the mend from a gunshot wound, and his return adds to a running back room that already features the SEC's leading rusher. Jamal Roberts became the conference's first back to surpass 1,000 yards for the season while rushing for 138 yards and a touchdown on 23 carries in a win over Arkansas. Roberts surpassed 200 yards in wins over Florida and Texas A&M last month. Gaining traction against Texas will be tough. No team has averaged more than four yards per rush attempt against Texas. College Football playoff implications: Texas' chance to reach the College Football Playoff will improve to 67.5% with a win, according to the CBS Sports CFB Forecaster. They will drop to 22.8% with a loss. If the Longhorns lose, they would need to win out against LSU, Arkansas and Texas A&M in order to potentially reach the 12-team field as a three-loss team. Missouri's chances to make the CFP will improve to 16.1% with a win. Those hopes would crater to 1.6% with a loss. The Tigers close with Georgia , Kentucky and Oklahoma . Texas vs. Missouri prediction, picks The best unit on this field is the Texas defense. Regardless of the health status of star edge rusher Collin Simmons, the Longhorns should be able to slow down a Missouri offense that hasn't faced a swarming unit of this caliber. If Arch Manning can just take care of the football like he did last week, Texas can lean on its defense, win the field position battle and put stress on a Missouri defense that showed real vulnerability in losses to Mississippi State and Ole Miss. The Tigers have been great at home the last few years, but they are a rung below Texas in overall talent level. picks.blurb: Texas vs Missouri Predictions: Can Longhorns Avoid Upset? Staff Picks and Scores Skip to main content SI.COM LONGHORNS NEWS 2025 Football Bracket FOOTBALL FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS 2023 FOOTBALL COMMITS SI.COM LONGHORNS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM LONGHORNS BB After getting to play their entire October slate in the Lone Star State, the Longhorns are once again leaving town for Columbia, Missouri, to take on the No. 18 Missouri Tigers. While fans may already be looking ahead to next week's highly anticipated Death Valley matchup, the Tigers are certainly not a team to overlook . They're coming off a 34-10 blowout win over Arkansas — albeit, it was against the Razorbacks — and steamrolled the same Florida team that stunned Texas with a second-half comeback just a few weeks ago. Saturday's matchup carries significant postseason implications , both for the College Football Playoff and the SEC championship race, as both teams enter with identical 3-2 conference records. Here’s how the Texas Longhorns On SI Staff sees this one playing out. Matt Galatzan Texas has gotten back on track over the last two weeks, but various shortcoming are still very prevelent. Texas has struggled along offensive line, and as a result, the running game has suffered. Those issues have also caused a cascading effect on the passing game, making for an inconsistent product. To make things worse, things on the injury front don't look good for the Horns. Kade Phillips, Ryan Wingo and Graceson Littleton are all banged up but should play, while Colin Simmons and Cam Coleman are less likely to play, and Hollywood Smothers and Nick Townsend were both lost for the year. Texas can overcome these issues if the defense continues to perform at a high level. Ole Miss showed the blueprint to shut down the Tigers ' offense. If Texas can stay on schedule on offense and avoid a third-quarter collapse, I think they can get it done. Texas 27, Missouri 20 Phoenix Haigis Texas has started to find their groove again with two major wins at home against Ole Miss and Mississippi State. The Longhorns now go back on the road against another ranked opponent in Missouri. As much momentum as Texas has going into this game, all the advantages matchup-wise go in favor of the Tigers. Texas is dealing with a significant amount of major injuries with the addition of running back Hollywood Smothers being out for the season while Missouri will see their running back Ahmad Hardy return for the first time this season. The Tigers are one of the best teams at home this year and have the best turnover margin in the SEC against a Lorghorns team that has had turnover issues this season. Although Texas is favored, the math tells a different story and could eliminate the Longhorns’ playoff chances. Zion Trammell Texas and Missouri have the makings of a defensive slugfest. It’ll be a cold morning in Columbia, Missouri, which could challenge the offenses. Both the Longhorns and Tigers rank in the top four in the SEC in average rushing yards allowed per game. Texas may need a big defensive play to win. I think Will Muschamp’s defense will deliver, and the Longhorns will win a close game on Saturday. However, this feels like the Arch legacy game that many have been begging to see. Perhaps it's also because that might be what HAS to happen, but I'm riding with believing in Manning in this one. Oct 31, 2026; Austin, Texas, USA; Texas Longhorns linebacker Rasheem Biles reacts after making a defensive stop during the second half against the Mississippi State Bulldogs at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. Scott Wachter-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Leo Barnes All things considered, I still like this Texas team. This will be a defensive dogfight. It won't be pretty, and it might even be a little boring at times — that is, if all you care about is high-flying action. And while the injury report isn't promising one bit, I still believe this Texas defense can be every bit as legitimate as it's proven itself to be. Stopping Missouri starts with shutting down the run game, and I fully expect Justin Cryer and Rasheem Biles to help answer the call. I could easily see either one leading the team in tackles by the time it's all said and done. Ultimately, Texas' ability to stonewall opposing offenses should be enough to keep the Tigers in check, giving its sometimes-average offense just enough breathing room to squeak out another win. That meeting was the 2017 Texas Bowl. What should scare Longhorns fans is the 2026 version is tinkering on the edge of a disappointing bowl like that. Especially if they can't beat a team like Missouri. The Tigers are a good team. It's easy to see Missouri winning on Saturday. They're ranked just 11 spots below Texas in the College Football Playoff rankings and have the same record. And Mizzou has home field advantage. Then why is Texas a -3.5-point favorite. Because a fully functioning Texas team is better than Missouri. But this Texas team isn't fully functioning. First, the injuries are starting to pile up. It was announced this week that the Longhorns have lost running back Hollywood Smothers and tight end Nick Townsend for the rest of the season. All-American right tackle Trevor Goosby is also out for the year. And UT has been without All-American EDGE Colin Simmons for weeks. In addition to trying to plug the injury holes, Texas coach Steve Sarkisian must also continue to work on the offense. At times it looks great. But its not trustworthy. Will Muschamp's defense will need to stand tall for a third game in a row if the offense can't get it going. Tommy Bresee's Prediction Texas walks into this Missouri game needing the win to feel confident about their CFP chance heading into LSU. Missouri is a relative unknown, with losses to both Mississippi schools but a dominating win over Florida. Jamal Roberts and the run game leads the way, averaging just over 160 rushing yards/game. Austin Simmons has become a riser in this upcoming NFL Draft, flashing his elite arm talent every week. Texas was able to get a win over Tennessee earlier this season, but I don't see this as a task that's comparable. Missouri is capable of performing at a high level on both sides of the ball, especially the front seven defensively. It's difficult to imagine this Texas offense to trade punches with Missouri, especially on the road, so I'll take the Tigers to possibly end Texas' CFP hopes. Final Score: Texas 20, Missouri 23 Jamie Gatlin's Prediction The Longhorns will take on Missouri this Saturday in their latest SEC clash. The Tigers are off to an impressive 6-2 start and, like Texas, are 3-2 in conference play. Texas will need Arch Manning to be at his best and for the defense to shine. Last week, the Longhorns defense held Mississippi State to three points and 187 total yards. If the Longhorns can replicate that performance, another win could be on the horizon. This should be a game that Texas can win as they look to improve their playoff odds. Final Score: Texas 31, Missouri 13 Trey Luerssen's Prediction When this year's schedule came out, I thought the game against Mizzou might be the toughest to forecast. But it's even tougher now, because we're not sure which team will actually show up on either side of the ball. Both teams have had some big wins and some real clunkers. How much will Texas miss Smothers and Townsend? Can the defense slow down the Tigers offense? Which version of quarterback Arch Manning will show up in Columbia? For four games in a row, Texas has jumped out to an early lead and then coughed it up by the end of the third quarter. UT is 2-2 in that stretch. A coin flip. Twice the dam broke and twice it didn't. I think the defense will save the offense again. picks.blurb: Texas Longhorns final odds and prediction for Week 10 vs. Missouri Tigers Skip to main content Recruiting Women's sports Men's Basketball Women's basketball Softball and Baseball Texas Longhorns history FanSided NCAA Sites In a rollercoaster of a season, the Texas Longhorns have righted the ship and are back on track to return to the College Football Playoff. However, there are four games remaining, and the first one up is a top-25 matchup on the road against the No. 18 Missouri Tigers. So, as the Horns look to cement their place in the postseason, what should we expect, and what are oddsmakers expecting, out of Texas? Well, despite the Horns struggling against lesser opponents throughout the season, and despite the fact that it's a road game for them, head coach Steve Sarkisian and his squad are favored in Columbia this Saturday. Final spread, moneyline, and total for No. 7 Texas at No. 18 Missouri Spread: -2.5 Texas, +2.5 Missouri Moneyline: -142 Texas, +120 Missouri Over-Under: +/-42.5 points While the spread hasn't changed throughout the week, with the Horns idling as 2.5-point favorites , the point total has dropped from the initial 44.5-point expectation. Now, the over-under is set at just 42.5 points, giving a nod to the two teams' defenses over their offenses and setting the final score somewhere in the ballpark of 22.5-20, with the Horns walking away victorious. For understanding the moneyline, one simply can't overthink what the numbers mean. If someone bet $142 on the Horns winning, they would walk away with a $100 profit. If they bet $100 on the Tigers winning, they would walk away with a $120 profit. Makes sense, right? Pick your champion (you can change it later). We’ll email you when brackets open. Keys to Longhorns defeating the Tigers in Week 10 So, in order for the Longhorns to pull off that narrow victory (or, hopefully, by a larger margin) over Missouri? Well, for starters, with both starting wide receivers Cam Coleman and Ryan Wingo possibly missing from the lineup, quarterback Arch Manning is going to have to either (1) connect with new downfield targets or (2) continue to use his legs more. Similarly, the Texas offense will have to lean on the run game, which has been hit or miss this season, despite the fact that the team's original RB1, Hollywood Smothers, has been sidelined for the season with a torn MCL. So, Raleek Brown and supporting running backs Michael Terry III and Derrek Cooper Jr. will have to step up to the plate to carry the load out of the backfield. The Horns are also struggling with injuries on the defensive side of the ball, possibly opening up the air-raid offense for the Tigers and quarterback Austin Simmons. However, even with the nation's top defensive player, Colin Simmons, still sidelined, Texas has continued to dominate at the line of scrimmage. In other words, this might be an even lower-scoring game than Vegas oddsmakers are expecting, especially if Texas struggles to find its footing right away on offense. On3's Pete Nakos first reported Thursday that Smothers won't play again this season, while 247Sports' Eric Henry confirmed the running back tore his MCL. The news arrived after Smothers suffered a knee injury in last weekend's 31-3 win over Mississippi State, with the running back having appeared in six of Texas' eight games this season. The former NC State transfer will complete the 2026 season with 69 carries for 283 yards and two touchdowns. He also caught 10 passes for 79 yards and another score. Smothers' rushing touchdowns came in the fourth quarter of Texas' comeback win over then-No. 1 Ohio State in Week 2, with the rusher failing to score in any of the other five games he played. The Longhorns running back battled multiple injuries throughout the season and missed two games before returning against Mississippi State. He finished that game with just four carries for minus-6 yards before being helped off the field. The timing adds pressure to the Manning-led offense as Texas enters the final month with little margin for error in the College Football Playoff race. The No. 7 Longhorns are 6-2 and still have games remaining against Missouri, LSU, Arkansas and Texas A&M. Texas visits No. 18 Missouri on Saturday at noon ET on ESPN. home.blurb: "We were very fortunate. When you watch it, it looks bad, but the cleat was not in the ground, which is a real relief there," Mizzou head coach Eli Drinkwitz said Tuesday. But, again, I don't know how his body will respond to that injury." The Tigers did, as expected, rule out defensive end Langden Kitchen, who Drinkwitz said Tuesday had surgery on his knee after sustaining an injury during the Tigers' loss to Texas this past Saturday. Kitchen will not play for Mizzou again this season. As it has since SEC play started, Mizzou ruled out running back Malae Fonoti, who is out for the season, right tackle Josh Atkins, who Eli Drinkwitz said he does not expect to be available this year, and tight end Gavin Hoffman. The possible designations, from most likely to play to least likely, are as follows: available; probable; questionable; doubtful; out. The reports are not technically injury reports, which some teams — Mizzou often included — provided in years prior. Instead, they are lists that include any players ruled unavailable or possibly unavailable for upcoming games. That could be for any number of reasons, including but not limited to injuries. Luckily, in Texas's final availability report ahead of kickoff, it looked like the Horns might actually catch a break as a few players shifted toward being available. Additionally, edge rusher Richard Wesley and tight end Nick Townsend were both on the availability report, once again, as "out." Wide receiver Cam Coleman joined Simmons in the grey area after getting beat up against Mississippi State last week. On ESPN's College GameDay , Pete Thamel reported that the two were "game-time decisions," with Simmons seeing a larger likelihood of suiting up and actually setting foot on the field. The only thing that scares me for the Gophers' chances this week is a hangover after last week's emotional loss to Indiana, but I expect Fleck's team to be ready to end UCLA's perfect season. And UCLA is coming to Minneapolis to play in 40-degree temps in a game that kicks off at 9 a.m. Pacific time. This will be another big win and field storm for P.J. Fleck. I think we'll see something similar with the Gophers' defense limiting a UCLA offense that is somehow averaging fewer passing yards than Minnesota this season. The Bruins have a top-15 run game, though, so Minnesota's defense will have its hands full there. This is going to be the question going forward: until proven otherwise, can the Gophers' offense do just enough to squeak out a win? LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings No. 5 Alabama is out to defend its College Football Playoff ranking, while No. 14 LSU seeks to remain in the hunt Getty Images One of the best modern-day rivalries in college football headlines on Saturday when No. 5 Alabama and No. 14 LSU meet in Baton Rouge for the 91st meeting in the series. The Crimson Tide hold a 58-27-5 advantage overall, but it's the 13-2 record in the past 15 meetings that has given them the upper hand in a battle between programs that would otherwise be considered peers. This is, after all, set to be the 25th time that both schools are inside the top 15 of the AP Top 25 poll and with Alabama's recent crowning as a top-five team in the College Football Playoff rankings, there's even more ranked-on-ranked intrigue. LSU is hoping that the home field advantage of Death Valley can play a role in the game, as the Tigers are 32-3 in their last 35 home games in Tiger Stadium. Speaking of streaks, the game also presents LSU coach Lane Kiffin with a chance to finally defeat Alabama as a head coach. The former Crimson Tide offensive coordinator lost to Nick Saban once as Tennessee's head coach in 2009, then four times between 2020-23 as Ole Miss ' head coach, when they were SEC West division rivals. That 0-5 record against the Crimson Tide, paired with LSU's recent struggles in the series, provides plenty of extra motivation for the home team looking to roar back into the playoff race. Where to watch Alabama vs. LSU live Date : Saturday, Nov. 7 | Time : 3:30 p.m. ET Location : Tiger Stadium -- Baton Rouge, Louisiana TV: ABC | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Alabama vs. LSU: Need to know Alabama's injury report will be an X-factor: There will be key updates throughout the week, perhaps all the way up to warm-ups, that will determine the health of the Crimson Tide and their ability to perform to the expectations of their top-five rating. Starting center Racin Delgatty has missed multiple games while dealing with injury, and his absence has been noticeable on an offensive line that has cooled off since putting up 49+ points in consecutive wins against Florida State , South Carolina and Mississippi State . The Crimson Tide have failed to record 70+ rushing yards as a team in each of their last two games and allowed 21 sacks in SEC play, which ranks 14th among 16 teams in the league. Alabama will also be looking for updates from star wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams and cornerback Zabien Brown , adding to the unknowns for how the Tide will stack up against LSU. LSU passing attack rounding into form : No one in the SEC had a more productive passing attack in the month of October than LSU, which averaged 339.5 passing yards across all four games last month. The Tigers went 3-1 across those games, only losing to top-10 Kentucky by one point in Lexington on a walk-off two-point try. LSU now leads the SEC and ranks tied for 7th nationally on the season, averaging 318.0 passing yards per game, and the improvements have come with both Sam Leavitt's improved play and the emergence of Jackson Harris as a go-to receiver. A transfer from Hawaii , Harris played three whole games before scoring his first touchdown of the season but has exploded ever since with seven touchdown catches across the last five games. That includes four multiple-touchdown games and a yards-per-reception average (17.6) that ranks 4th among all SEC pass catchers. Kalen DeBoer set up in some favorable situational spots : When Alabama hired Kalen DeBoer away from Washington to take over in Tuscaloosa after Nick Saban's retirement, his track record as a big-time, high-leverage coach met the demands of the job. Since Alabama is almost always playing in high-pressure games against quality opponents, the school needed to know that Saban's successor would be ready for those moments. Currently, DeBoer is 21-8 against AP-ranked teams as a head coach, which is the fourth-best record in AP poll history with a minimum of 20 games coached (.724 winning percentage). His company on that list, for those unaware, is one spot behind Urban Meyer (.746) and one spot ahead of Kirby Smart (.710). DeBoer has also won eight straight games after a bye, with the last defeat in this spot coming in 2020 as the head coach of Fresno State . Alabama vs. LSU prediction, picks While the combination of LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt and Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell provides the potential for plenty of points, this game could end up being decided by both defenses. Alabama's offensive injuries have clearly limited their ability to execute on schedule, and LSU's defense represents the best test they've faced since the loss at Tennessee. In the same manner, LSU's pass attack could set them up for some of the turnovers that have powered Alabama's excellence this season (+7 turnover margin is tied for 11th nationally) and prevent touchdowns even after successful drives. All in all, it points to a lower-scoring classic, where I'll favor the home team to make big plays late. picks.blurb: CFP Rankings Prediction: How Far Could LSU Fall After Loss to Alabama? Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM TIGERS FB SI.COM TIGERS BB With three losses on the season, the LSU Tigers find themselves in a rough spot in an attempt to make the College Football Playoff this season. After being dismantled at home by the Alabama Crimson Tide , reaching the coveted post-season seems unlikely in year one of the Lane Kiffin era, and there is another top-ranked team waiting just around the corner for the Tigers. Having already fallen in the AP Pol l, to nearly on the outside looking in, where will the Tigers find themselves in the second College Football Playoff rankings ? With two losses already on the year heading into the first set of College Football Playoff rankings, the Tigers' room for error was minimal, and their ranking reflected that, coming in at No. 14. A win over the Crimson Tide would have put the Tigers in a comfortable position for the rest of the year, especially given the rest of the schedule remaining. Instead, with three losses, their ranking will plummet during the second release. Despite the loss, the Tigers shouldn't fall out of the top 25, as the committee has proven it won't shy away from ranking three-loss teams. Three were ranked last week: the South Carolina Gamecocks, the Oregon Ducks, and the Florida Gators. The Tigers should, at a minimum, replace the Gators, who suffered a fourth loss of the season this past weekend. The Missouri Tigers, who were also ranked and lost a third game of the season, should fall, but they also played a closer game against the top-ranked Texas Longhorns. The Ohio State Buckeyes will plummet as well, and they entered the weekend ranked higher than the Tigers. Considering those two teams, and the inclusion of potentially the New Mexico Lobos, who continue to find ways to win this season, there are a handful of teams fighting for fewer spots than available. With that said, the Tigers, just based on team talent alone, and every win being dominant so far this year, should be around No. 22-25, probably right at No. 24, providing another ranked SEC matchup this weekend against the Texas Longhorns.
