Our Alabama vs. LSU prediction and college football picks back Lane Kiffin and the Tigers to snap their Saban Bowl losing streak as Alabama seeks its fourth straight series victory on the first Saturday in November. The Crimson Tide visit Tiger Stadium in Baton Rouge, La., where LSU enters as a 5. 5-point favorite in Death Valley. Kickoff is scheduled for 3: 30 p. m. ET on ABC on Saturday, Nov. 7. TOP PICK Who will win Alabama vs LSU: LSU -5.5 The last time LSU won the Saban Bowl, Nick Saban was Alabama's head coach and Lane Kiffin was still beloved at Ole Miss . That will change Saturday when Kiffin's surging Tigers take advantage of a Crimson Tide team that's looked like a far cry from its No. 5 College Football Playoff ranking. With LSU's defensive ferocity and Alabama's offensive struggles, I like the Tigers to cover up to -6.5 at home against the Tide. Not only has LSU's defense been wrecking opponents, but the Tigers' offense has been on fire too, with Sam Leavitt fourth nationally in QBR (85.3) and 12th in adjusted completion percentage (79.5%). Leavitt's improved play and the emergence of Jackson Harris (480 receiving yards and seven TDs in his last four SEC games) are a problem for an Alabama defense that's ranked 78th in pass success rate (44.3%). LSU's defense is especially loaded, and with Alabama's struggles against quality defenses, I would play the Under at 51.5 or better. The Tigers are second nationally in sacks (34) , and Keelon Russell hasn't managed pressure well. He's been sacked the ninth-most in the country (22) and has a 20.4% pressure-to-sack rate. But I don't expect an offensive onslaught from LSU either. This is the best defense the Tigers have faced this season, with Alabama ranking 20th nationally in available yards percentage (37.7%) and 14th in net adjusted EPA per play. The Crimson Tide have faced two high-quality defenses this season and failed to score more than 17 points in both games. Alabama continues to deal with two key injuries on the offensive side of the ball, with both center Racin Delgatty and wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams questionable for this game. If those two don't play, Alabama will struggle to score even 20 points. The Crimson Tide don't have consistent playmakers outside of Coleman-Williams, and LSU's defense brings the heat, ranking fourth nationally in havoc rate (22.2%) . Death Valley is one of the hardest places to play, and with Alabama's broken offense, I don't expect the Tide to score much early against this opportunistic LSU defense. (Photo by Stew Milne/Getty Images) | Getty Images Joshua Chatham · SB Nation Fri, November 6, 2026 at 3:18 PM UTC · 8 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Happy Friday, everyone. The women's basketball team feasted on yet another cupcake last night to move to 3-0, this time taking down Alabama A&M by a 96-43 margin . The men play tonight against Arkansas State, and we will have coverage of that one later on. Alabama football plays at LSU tomorrow, as you well know. Your previews: Alabama gets an immediate chance to justify its CFP ranking, while LSU can strengthen its argument with a win that leaves the Tide staring at three losses. I picked LSU to win this game in August, and I'm sticking with the Tigers' passing game at home against an Alabama secondary still sorting through injuries. Sam Leavitt throws for 278 yards and two touchdowns, and Jackson Harris catches both of them while finishing with 110 receiving yards. LSU wins 26-20, keeping its SEC title hopes alive and giving Alabama fans another reason to avoid the internet. Alabama football needs this win. Kalen DeBoer wins after idle weeks. And the Crimson Tide knows how to win against LSU on the road. All of these remain true. But this is a new Tigers team in a new era with Lane Kiffin at the helm. It's a unit starting to find itself after single-score losses to Ole Miss and Kentucky. LSU has the second best scoring offense and defense in the SEC. It has the No. 1 total offense and defense in the SEC. This is a Tigers team that is waiting for an opportunity to see what it can do against the upper echelon of SEC play in November, and the Crimson Tide is the first team in LSU's way. Alabama has looked like the best team in the country before on the road, beating Mississippi State to a pulp in Starkville, but the same couldn't be said about Kentucky in Lexington, or, especially, Tennessee in Knoxville. Expect the Crimson Tide to falter against LSU. Prediction: No. 15 LSU 31, No. 9 Alabama 24 While the combination of LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt and Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell provides the potential for plenty of points, this game could end up being decided by both defenses. Alabama's offensive injuries have clearly limited their ability to execute on schedule, and LSU's defense represents the best test they've faced since the loss at Tennessee. In the same manner, LSU's pass attack could set them up for some of the turnovers that have powered Alabama's excellence this season (+7 turnover margin is tied for 11th nationally) and prevent touchdowns even after successful drives. All in all, it points to a lower-scoring classic, where I'll favor the home team to make big plays late. LSU is a completely different animal in Baton Rouge. It's an afternoon game instead of an ultra-amped up night showdown in Death Valley, but it shouldn't matter too much that the Tiger fan base is just a little less … prepared. Yeah, Ole Miss, Kentucky, and Auburn are, arguably, the three best teams LSU faced, which is why those road games were tough, but LSU hasn't even let the opponents breathe at home, winning all five games by a combined score of 225-44 with the closest game a 35-6 win over Texas A&M. LSU won't destroy Alabama, and it'll be a back-and-forth fight, but there will be that moment in the second half when it all clicks, and the Tigers will put the game away with a sharp scoring drive. The crowd will take over from there. LSU 30, Alabama 23 John Brice: LSU Matt Hayes: LSU Jordan Mendoza: Alabama Paul Myerberg: LSU Erick Smith: Alabama Eddie Timanus: LSU Blake Toppmeyer: LSU Craig Meyer: Alabama 31, LSU 27 LSU 35, Alabama 28: Tigers quarterback Sam Leavitt was flat out bad in his first three games: He threw three touchdowns and five interceptions against Clemson, Louisiana Tech and Ole Miss. Since then, he has completed 75.4% of his passes and has vastly reduced his turnovers as he's adjusted to coach Lane Kiffin's system. Keelon Russell can get just as hot for the Crimson Tide. We just haven't seen as much of that lately, so we'll lean toward Leavitt and Co. here. — Adam Bittner, USA TODAY This LSU team continues to impress. They now enter Week 10 ranking first in the entire country in net adjusted EPA per play, seventh in net yards per play, and seventh in net success rate. That's a step above Alabama, which ranks fifth, 15th, and ninth in those three metrics. The one weakness that LSU has is stopping the run, ranking just 54th in opponent EPA per rush, but unfortunately for the Crimson Tide, they haven't run the ball efficiently this season, ranking just 50th in EPA per rush. Without the ability to take advantage of LSU's biggest weakness, this is going to be a tough road game for Alabama. I'll lay the points with the Tigers. The sportsbooks have LSU laying nearly a touchdown at home against Alabama. That means at a neutral site, LSU would be favored by roughly a field goal, so Las Vegas believes the Tigers are the better team. While LSU has played better of late, and I would anticipate Lane Kiffin dialing up some trickeration in this game, LSU hasn't beaten Alabama since 2022 and Kiffin historically has struggled against the Tide. Give me Alabama to win a close one inside Tiger Stadium Saturday. Alabama 24, LSU 21 That last one is from The Daily Advertiser. We see what you're trying to pull, bro. There is no reason whatsoever for Alabama fans to have much confidence in this one. We have a third of the starting lineup listed as questionable, and we saw what happened in Knoxville when none of those guys played. Word is that Alabama expects to get some key players back, but will they be 100%? On top of that, Keelon Russell has struggled at times against the blitz this season, and will be facing one of the most blitz-happy teams in the country. It does appear that LSU will be without MLB Whit Weeks, so that will help. Still, this is perhaps the most hostile environment in the sport, against a team that leads the SEC in both offense and defense, that also happens to need this win to get into the playoff discussion after Tuesday night's rankings dropped. Sure, they are in this position because they lost at Ole Miss and Kentucky, but those were road games. Still, we Gump to a standard around here. The one thing that Alabama can point to is Sam Leavitt's propensity to turn the ball over, and Alabama's defense has been as opportunistic as any in the country. We're going to say that the bye week afforded Russell the opportunity to learn from film study, and Alabama will get just enough guys back to get it done in Red Stick as they have so many times in the past. Leavitt has two picks, including one returned for a touchdown, and Alabama wins 30-27. That is merely my hopium, of course. Let us know your thoughts in the comments. Matt Stahl correctly notes that Alabama needs explosive plays in the passing game to win this one. Ryan Coleman-Williams is on the road to recovery, but was still listed as questionable for LSU after missing the Tennessee and Texas A&M games. Tiger head coach Lane Kiffin predicted Thursday that the junior wideout will play, but that isn't guaranteed. Coleman-Williams can provide an explosive play threat whenever he's on the field. Against Tennessee, that lack of explosives was obvious, and contributed to the loss. That same thing can't happen in Tiger Stadium. Even if its superstar receiver can't go, Alabama has to find some big plays on offense. Lotzeir Brooks is a threat, as is Rico Scott. The Crimson Tide could also find explosives from the likes of Derek Meadows and Cederian Morgan at receiver. There always needs to be a semblance of balance, but this is not a "run the ball" game. LSU leads the SEC in rushing defense, allowing only 2.7 yards per carry and 85 yards per contest. In order to push the ball down the field, Alabama's tackles will have to neutralize DE Princewill Umanmielen. Alabama has faced some prominent pass-rushers this season, but LSU defensive end Princewill Umanmielen has a strong argument to be the best. Umanmielen's 8.5 sacks rank fifth in the country, while his 12 tackles for loss are tied for ninth. The senior is second in the SEC in each of these stat categories. There have been numerous instances this season where Crimson Tide quarterback Keelon Russell has held the ball for too long, and giving any edge to Umanmielen, along with the rest of LSU's pass-rush — which leads the country in sacks per game (4.4) — will make it very difficult for Alabama to come out on top. None of this will be easy. That's about it for today. Have a great weekend.

Both teams are heading into the high-stakes matchup after a rested bye week as both teams work on their list of player injuries. The game's outcome could decide both teams' fates in the playoffs, creating an anticipated matchup in the long-standing rivalry. Here are three bold predictions for LSU's matchup against Alabama. LSU Tigers lead Auburn Tigers 31-10 at halftime. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect LSU is able to recover from some of its injuries, including tight end Trey'Dez Green , who returns after missing four of the team's mid-season games. Green appeared in the team's defeat over Auburn, putting up 50 receiving yards across five receptions and a touchdown. Green ended up leaving the game early, after head coach Lane Kiffin reported that Auburn's defense was attempting hip drop tackles on the talented tight end, a move that significantly increases a player's chances of getting injured and one that was banned in the NFL in 2024. While he may not be getting targeted in the same way against Alabama, he still will have all the pressure on him, making him a risky target for Leavitt, who's already struggled with turnovers this season. The 6'7, 237 lb. tight end is the ultimate weapon on offense, one that Alabama has experience in facing, being aware of his ability to contribute to the Tigers' offensive success and making all the moves to limit it on Saturday. LSU's Defense Will Hold Keelon Russell To 170 Passing Yards Oct 24, 2026; Tuscaloosa, AL, USA; Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell (12) leaves the field after the Crimson Tide win at Saban Field at Bryant Denny Stadium. Russell is also anticipating the obstacle of the Bayou Bandits, a team that has allowed 172.8 passing yards from opponents per game. Limiting Russell to the magic number of 170 passing yards will prove its ability to hit Alabama where it hurts, putting pressure on its offensive leader. During the team's back-to-back losses this season against Georgia and Tennessee, Russell put up a season low of 147 passing yards during the trip to Neyland Stadium, scoring the only touchdown for the Tide during the game. Against the Bulldogs, Russell still couldn't hit the 200 mark, ending the loss with 185 passing yards. Now that he will face one of the league's most dangerous defenses, a unit that once held the most sacks this season, Russell's passing production could take another major blow if the defense can keep up the pressure all game long. LSU Will Record 5+ Sacks Oct 24, 2026; Auburn, Alabama, USA; LSU Tigers defensive end Princewill Umanmielen (1) sacks Auburn Tigers quarterback Byrum Brown (17) during the second half at Jordan-Hare Stadium. Mandatory Credit: John Reed-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect LSU's defense can limit Russell's production from the first snap, closing in on him in the pocket and recording more than five sacks against the Tide quarterback. He sits in the Top-10 for the quarterback with the most sacks this season, recording a staggering 22 so far. Against LSU's defense - a unit that met the program's record for the most sacks in one game during Week 2 of the season - Russell and his offensive line could be in major trouble. This production will come from the exterior of the line, with defensive end Princewill Umanmielen becoming Russell's biggest nightmare as the leader of the defense with nine sacks so far. Even if the Crimson Tide can put extra pressure on Umanmielen's side, defensive end Jordan Ross brings the same threat on the opposite end, as major pressure will be closing in on Russell all game long. away.blurb: Alabama (7-2, 5-2) played like its season depended on it, jumping out to a first-half lead and overpowering the Tigers in their own home for a 31-13 victory. Freshman quarterback Kaelon Russell put on a show, throwing for 206 yards and three touchdowns, picking LSU’s defense apart when it matter most. Despite being outgained in total yards of offense, the Crimson Tide made the most of every red zone trip they had, while the same couldn’t be said for Lane Kiffin and his Tigers. LSU ended the game going 2 out of 4 in its red zone visits, with both of those red zone trips ending in field goals instead of touchdowns. With this loss, LSU falls to .500 in conference play and possibly out of playoff contention. Kiffin and the Tigers will look to flush this one quickly with No. 10 Texas coming to town on Nov. 14. The story of this game will come down to which quarterback can perform better. Sam Leavitt has been better for the Tigers (6-2, 3-2 SEC) of late. His las time out at Auburn, he threw for 387 yards, accounted for four touchdowns but arguably more important, he didn't have a turnover. After a 32-yard punt return from Coleman-Williams, Russell only needed one play to extend Alabama's lead in the fourth quarter. The freshman signal caller dropped a dime from 25 yards out to wide receiver Cederian Morgan for a touchdown. The play only took five second off the clock, a good thing for LSU who now has even more of a hill to climb to make a comeback. LSU's defense was never in position on that drive and got burned twice. That's one of the few times all season Blake Baker's defense looked befuddled and out of place. Leavitt and company came out of the halftime looking to put points on the board. While they still have yet to taste the endzone, Leavitt and running back Dillin Jones were able to get the Tigers back in scoring position on their opening second-half drive. Staryzk capped the drive off with a 41-yard field goal to make it a four-point game. LSU faced a fourth and long to start the second quarter and elected to trust in Staryzk's foot to give it the lead. Staryzk attempted a field goal from 56 yards out and pushed it far left for his first miss of the day. home.headline: Whit Weeks and another injured LSU defender could return for Texas game, according to SEC report
home.blurb: Whit Weeks and another injured LSU defender could return for Texas game, according to SEC report By JON BLAU | Staff writer Jon Blau Weeks was categorized as “questionable” for the Tigers’ game against Texas in the Southeastern Conference’s initial release for the week. The senior defender has been sidelined since he suffered a lower-leg injury against Texas A&M on Sept. 26. Weeks was listed as “doubtful” on multiple SEC availability reports in the days leading up to last week’s game against Alabama. The senior was inevitably ruled out the Friday night before a 31-13 loss. LSU could also return another injured defender this Saturday, because defensive end Gabriel Reliford, who suffered an ACL tear in March during spring practice, was listed as probable for the Texas game. LSU coach Lane Kiffin previously said it was unlikely Reliford would return to play this season. Right tackle Weston Davis, who was knocked out by an injury versus Alabama, was also listed as probable for Texas. A listing of “questionable” is supposed to confer that an athlete has about a 50% chance of suiting up for that week’s game. “Doubtful” means closer to a 25% chance — and an “out” designation means a player has been ruled out completely. Aside from Weeks, LSU is without safety Dashawn Spears, receiver Phillip Wright and linebacker Charles Ross, who have all suffered season-ending injuries. But the Tigers remain relatively healthy otherwise, especially since tight end Trey’Dez Green’s return. Freshman defensive tackle Richard Anderson, who missed the Auburn and Alabama contests, was also listed as out on Wednesday’s report. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings No. 12 Ohio State hosts No. 23 Oregon in a pivotal game in the Big Ten and CFP race Getty Images Week 10 of the college football season has been highlighted since the schedule was released, with No. 23 Oregon's trip to face No. 12 Ohio State among the headliners. However, when the Buckeyes host the Ducks at 3:30 p.m. ET on CBS, it will not be two teams vying for a bye in the College Football Playoff, but instead two programs trying to keep their season from unraveling. The Ducks, at 5-3, have already seen their playoff dreams snuffed out, but a win last week against Northwestern brought their offense to life after a coordinator change. Dylan Raiola had his best game as a starter for Oregon in a win over Northwestern, and now the Ducks have real belief they can go into the Horseshoe and pick up a win that could salvage what's been a disappointing season. Ohio State, meanwhile, comes in with a backup quarterback of their own and is searching for answers after a 30-18 loss on the road to USC last week. Luke Fahey will get his second start and first at home, hoping to find more success and keep Ohio State in the playoff hunt after the first CFP rankings put them at No. 12 -- which would be the first team out of the 12-team playoff. The winner on Saturday will enter the stretch run of the season feeling like they've stabilized after a shock to the system in the form of losing their star quarterbacks for the year. The loser, on the other hand, will realize their goals are no longer within reach and face some hard questions entering the offseason. Where to watch Ohio State vs. Oregon live Date : Saturday, Nov. 7 | Time : 3:30 p.m. ET Location : Ohio Stadium -- Columbus, Ohio TV: CBS | Live stream: CBSSports.com , CBS Sports App Streaming on Paramount+ Premium Ohio State vs. Oregon: Need to know Can Ohio State solve red-zone woes?: The Buckeyes moved the ball fine against USC's defense. It was the best rushing performance from Ohio State this season in Big Ten play in terms of yards per carry (4.74), and while Fahey missed some explosives, he still threw for 260 yards. The problem for Ohio State was finishing drives with six points instead of three. Ohio State made four trips into the red zone against USC and came away with just 13 points. Against Indiana , it also scored 13 points in three trips to the red zone, and the inability to come away with touchdowns nearly cost them there too. If the Buckeyes are going to control this game and keep Oregon from building belief it can win on the road, Fahey has to be sharper in the red zone and the Ohio State rushing attack has to be able to help out. Ducks find life after coordinator change: Oregon's offense had its best performance since the win at USC last Saturday afternoon against Northwestern, one week after firing offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer. Interim coordinator Jay Johnson seemed able to get Raiola into a rhythm and keep him there, something the Ducks have struggled with all season (even with Dante Moore ). The frustration after the Illinois game seemed to be an unwillingness to stick with what worked -- in that game, it was the rushing attack -- and against Northwestern, once they found some concepts that worked, they went back to the well until proven otherwise. That seems simple, but it's not always easy as a play-caller to not let your mind wander and get too cute trying to stay ahead of the defense. Johnson seems more comfortable just rolling with what works and being aggressive in any spot, which seems to have a trickle-down effect on Raiola and the offense, also playing with more comfort and aggression. That's going to be necessary against an Ohio State defense that is quite good but, as USC proved, can be hit for big plays. Oregon can't be afraid to take swings as a road dog, and last week's performance gives it some confidence it can do that effectively with Raiola. Which defense can steal possessions?: With a young quarterback and a red-zone offense that's struggling, the Buckeyes might need their defense to give them a spark. For as good as the Buckeyes have been defensively this season, they haven't been great at turning teams over. They have just four interceptions on the year (94th nationally) and are 48th in total turnovers forced at 11. Raiola has been prone to turnovers for his entire career dating back to Nebraska and will likely present a couple of opportunities -- either with interceptable balls or strip sacks -- for the Buckeyes to steal a possession or two. Ohio State has to capitalize on those chances if they want to help their sputtering offense. On the other side, the best way to make Ohio State tight in this one would be to pick off the young quarterback and make Ryan Day a bit anxious about letting the young man sling it. Oregon has nine interceptions this season (13th in the country), and if they can bait the freshman into an early mistake, it could alter the Buckeyes' game plan and give the Ducks an even better opportunity on the road. Ohio State vs. Oregon prediction, picks The Ducks have to pick up where they left off offensively to have a chance here, and they should push the tempo a bit and try to stretch things out in the air. Ohio State should be able to run the ball well, and at home I would expect Fahey and the offense to operate a bit better in the red zone to put touchdowns on the board when they do move the ball. A Ducks offense trying to push it in the passing game should result in big plays (possibly for both teams), and this is a rare big game where I'm anticipating plenty of points. Ohio State (6-2, 4-1 Big Ten) is back in Columbus in a must-win spot against the Oregon Ducks (5-3, 3-2 Big Ten) for both their conference title and playoff lives. What was thought to be a matchup of national title-contending heavyweights is far different, and only one can remain near the top of a crowded league. Find out whether our On SI crew is backing the Buckeyes as kickoff and the game are underway. Ohio State so far this season: 6-2 (4-1 Big Ten) Zain Bando : 7-1 Dylan Buganski : 6-2 Rafael Zamorano : 4-2 (no pick in Week 6 or Week 7) Chip Minnich : 5-1 (began contributing ahead of Week 3) Zain Bando: Ohio State 24, Oregon 16 If the Buckeyes needed a wake-up call, last week was it. Now they find themselves with their back against the wall, likely needing to run the table to go back to Indianapolis for the second straight season. Before they can focus on that, however, they need to knock off Oregon, which still has a chance to be one-half of the championship game if things break the Ducks’ way despite three losses (including an outright upset against Illinois in late October). Last week, Oregon overcame a 14-point deficit to beat Northwestern and protect home-field advantage. This week, Ohio State can’t fall into a similar trap by getting comfortable with an early lead. There could be a chaotic finish in this one, and if Ohio State has the ball last, its chances to win and remain prevalent in the Big Ten title race will be very much alive. But only time will tell. Rafael Zamorano: Ohio State 23, Oregon 21 It might not be a do-or-die moment yet for Ohio State, currently ranked 12th in the nation with four games left on the schedule, but it sure feels like one. And, as it’s been for most of the year, expect Jeremiah Smith to receive most of the targets on offense -- although it seems pretty clear that the Buckeyes could benefit from spreading the ball around a little more to keep defenses honest. Having said that, dropping a third regular-season game this Saturday against Oregon would no doubt shrink the Buckeyes’ playoff chances dramatically Luckily for Ohio State, Oregon’s season hasn’t turned out as expected either, after starting off as the No. 2-ranked team in the land, one spot behind the Buckeyes. On paper, Oregon might still be the most formidable opponent left on the season calendar, but these aren’t the same Ducks widely projected to be competing for a Natty just a couple of months ago. Ohio State will need to show a ton of improvement in the passing game, especially when it comes to getting true freshman quarterback Luke Fahey into a rhythm. I see the Buckeyes getting back to the win column in a tight one. Chip Minnich: Ohio State 28, Oregon 24 "Desperate Measures” would be the title of this game if it were a movie. Ohio State sits at 6-2, Oregon at 5-3, and it is a legitimate point to make that the loser of this game could be on the outside looking in at The College Football Playoff. While people are understandably concerned about the play of Luke Fahey, Ohio State’s loss at USC last week was more on the defensive side of the ball, and Oregon has many talented players who should have Ohio State defensive coordinator Matt Patricia burning the midnight oil in preparation this week. If there is a bright spot, Oregon QB Dylan Raiola has shown a tendency to turn the ball over, so perhaps Coach Patricia will turn up the pressure to force some mistakes. Field position will be at a premium. Brace yourselves, Ohio State fans — Oregon has even more talent on the defensive line than USC does, so it will be imperative that Fahey gets the ball out quickly, or at least runs for positive yardage when and if the pocket breaks down. Kicking field goals may be crucial in this one, even though Ohio State understandably wants touchdowns. Here's hoping that Ohio State has been working on their red zone woes. I believe it will be a back-and-forth, and this is the type of game that feels like whichever team has the ball last will have the opportunity to win it in the final moments. Give me Ohio State in a nail-biter. Dylan Buganski: Ohio State 20, USC 17 Coming into the 2026 college football season, this was penciled early on as one of the most impactful games of the season, with both teams expected to be in the top 10, with heavy Big Ten implications on the line. Oh, how things can change quickly in a short two months. Oregon is basically out of the playoff picture, while Ohio State’s chances are hanging on by a thread. This still sets the stage for a dramatic 3:30 kickoff this Saturday in Columbus, with the Buckeyes needing to answer a lot of questions after a 30-18 loss at USC last week. The defense should be stronger for Ohio State in this matchup, cleaning up mistakes that cost them against the Trojans and causing turnovers against an inconsistent Oregon offense. Yet, playmakers Evan Stewart and Dakorien Moore can turn a big play out of nowhere, and the Buckeyes have shown they are susceptible to it. Oregon is able to cash in on a few big plays, with their defense making this game a sweat. Yet, the budding run game and a clean game from freshman quarterback Luke Fahey does just enough for Ohio State to escape this game with a win, and playoff hopes that stay alive heading into their final three games of the season. The Buckeyes' five-game winning streak ended against USC last weekend, with backup quarterback Luke Fahey leading the team to just 18 points. Starting quarterback Julian Sayin will be sidelined once again this weekend as he continues to rehab an elbow injury suffered in the team's Week 7 win over Indiana. However, there are reasons to believe Ohio State will get back into the win column. Scoring just 18 points looks bad on the surface, but Fahey played relatively well against the Trojans in Week 9. He completed 15 of 25 passes from a clean pocket and held his own under pressure, completing 6 of 13 attempts without any turnover-worthy throws . Fahey looked much better than he did during his relief appearance against the Hoosiers, and it stands to reason that he'll look even better at home after another full week of practice. Coach Dan Lanning's squad received encouraging news this week with the star wide receiver Jeremiah McClellan listed as probable to return for what is essentially a must-win game. Sep 5, 2026; Eugene, Oregon, USA; Oregon Ducks wide receiver Jeremiah McClellan celebrates with teammates against the Boise State Broncos at Autzen Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Troy Wayrynen-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Buckeyes, who are coming off a 30-18 loss to USC, turn to backup quarterback Luke Fahey for a second consecutive week. Oregon debuted at No. 23 in the first College Football Playoff rankings, but a third conference loss would almost certainly doom the Ducks' College Football Playoff aspirations. Meanwhile, a second straight loss for Ohio State would further complicate the Buckeyes' path to the Big Ten Championship and CFP. Getting Jeremiah McClellan Up to Speed Sep 18, 2026; Eugene, Oregon, USA; Oregon Ducks wide receiver Jeremiah McClellan warms up before facing the Portland State Vikings at Autzen Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Troy Wayrynen-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Oregon quarterback Dylan Raiola versus Ohio State's Fahey isn't exactly the matchup people expected when this game was circled on many calendars before the season. It's been an up-and-down ride for Raiola, who has helped Oregon win three of its five games since quarterback Dante Moore suffered a concussion in Week 4 against USC. Raiola has thrown for 641 yards and four touchdowns in the last nine quarters. Now he likely gets McClellan back in the rotation, who caught seven passes for 170 yards and a touchdown during the first two games of the season before a broken foot sidelined him ahead of Portland State in Week 3. McClellan's return gives Oregon another offensive weapon as the Ducks contend with injuries in the backfield. Running back Brandon Smith stepped up against Northwestern, rushing for 82 yards and the go-ahead score with starting running backs Jordon Davison and Dierre Hill Jr. sidelined with injuries. The true freshman will likely hear his number called often once again versus Ohio State, with Davison ruled out and Hill Jr. expected to return after missing the second half against Northwestern. They'll need all healthy hands on deck this Saturday. The Buckeyes rank No. 11 nationally in total defense, allowing just 273.5 yards per game, including 177.8 passing yards and 95.8 rushing yards. Slowing Down Jeremiah Smith Oct. 31, 2026; Los Angeles; Ohio State Buckeyes wide receiver Jeremiah Smith runs back to the line of scrimmage against the USC Trojans at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect While the Oregon offense works to integrate McClellan back into its lineup, the Ducks defense will have its hands full with Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith. The junior's 1,067 receiving yards and 13 touchdowns rank second nationally behind only Oregon State wide receiver Jesse Legree (1,110 yards, 14 touchdowns), firmly placing Smith in the Heisman Trophy conversation. Smith has already proven a rapport with Fahey, catching 10 passes for 83 of the quarterback's 260 passing yards against USC in Fahey's first career start. Oct 31, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Ohio State Buckeyes quarterback Luke Fahey drops back against the Southern California Trojans at United Airlines Field at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The duo's 1-yard scoring connection against the Trojans was Smith's 40th touchdown with the Buckeyes to set the new Big Ten career mark. Oregon is surrendering an average of 341.8 total yards (208 passing) and 21.4 points per game. Yet, the Ducks tied for No. 13 with nine interceptions and No. 5 with 49 passes defended, including nine by cornerback Ify Ibidegwu, who leads the team. "He's big, physical, fast," Obidegwu said of Smith. "We're big, we're physical, fast corners, so it's a good matchup for sure. We're definitely excited and ready to go, for sure." Prediction and Betting Odds Jan. 1, 2025; Pasadena, California; Ohio State Buckeyes wide receiver Jeremiah Smith celebrates a first down catch against the Oregon Ducks at the Rose Bowl. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Ohio State enters Saturday's tilt at the Horseshoe as an 8-point favorite with a 44.5 over/under, per BetMGM. Oregon appears to have some new life with the recent improvement of Raiola and the offense since assistant quarterbacks coach Jay Johnson took over play-calling duties before the Northwestern game. Despite an inexperienced quarterback, Ohio State counters with an elite defense and Smith's game-changing potential. Throw in home field advantage and the Buckeyes eke out a 27-24 win over Lanning's squad, effectively ending the Ducks College Football Playoff hopes. In the long history of this rivalry, there's a good case that this is the biggest game ever. In his first year on the job, Will Stein has led Kentucky to a 7-1 start and a great shot at reaching the College Football Playoff with just four games remaining. His major transfer portal additions -- particularly quarterback Kenny Minchey and the offensive line -- clicked almost immediately. To this point, the Wildcats have passed all but one test they've faced, but the level of difficulty rises this weekend. Kentucky must continue to play clean football if it wants to come away with a win in Knoxville. Tennessee had two weeks to wallow in the "what if" after its three-point loss to South Carolina , but the team has to get back in the saddle this weekend. The Volunteers have the chance to pick up their second top-10 win of the season, which would really boost their CFP rankings. There's no doubt that the Vols have a playoff-caliber defense and running game, but can Josh Heupel fix the passing attack? Tennessee must improve there to reach its ceiling. Here is everything you need to know about this top-15 rivalry matchup in Knoxville. Tennessee vs. Kentucky: Need to know Rare ranked matchup: These teams have met well over 100 times, but this is just the fourth ranked matchup in history. Most recently, Tennessee and Kentucky played a top-25 matchup in 2022, with the Volunteers winning in a blowout. Prior to that, the only times the Vols and Wildcats were ranked simultaneously were in 1950 and 1951. That means there's a very good case for this matchup to be the biggest in the history of this rivalry. Games with stakes in this series usually go the way of Tennessee, but can Stein turn the tables on Saturday night? Kentucky not in the giving spirit: The holidays are approaching quickly, but Kentucky has not been feeling very generous. One of the driving factors behind the Wildcats' success is their incredible plus-13 turnover margin. That ranks first in the SEC and fourth in the entire country. For the first time since 2013, Kentucky has avoided turning the ball over in three consecutive games. If any team can end that streak, it's probably Tennessee, which has a great defense and has forced 14 turnovers in eight games. The Vols just have to protect the ball on offense. Heavy dose of DeSean Bishop : Kentucky defensive coordinator Jay Bateman probably doesn't need my advice, but I would suggest he lock in on Tennessee running back DeSean Bishop. He's been the engine of the Vols offense, and his 957 rushing yards rank sixth in the country. His 12 rushing touchdowns are tied for ninth. Over the last four games, Bishop has averaged 29 carries and 159 yards. If the Wildcats can contain Bishop and force Tennessee to throw the ball, that could be a recipe for success, but only one team has effectively shut Bishop down to this point. Pictured: Tennessee running back DeSean Bishop Ryan Minion · Action Network Sat, November 7, 2026 at 9:58 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Kentucky Wildcats take on the Tennessee Volunteers in Knoxville, Tennessee, on Saturday, Nov. 7. Kickoff is set for 6:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. Despite entering Saturday's Week 10 clash with a 7-1 overall record on the season, Kentucky remains a 6.5-point road underdog with a +188 price tag to pull off the outright upset. Tennessee is favored by 5.5 points on the spread with a moneyline of -220. Kentucky is a 5.5-point underdog with a moneyline of +184. The total is set at 49.5 points (-110 / -110). Here's my Kentucky vs. Tennessee prediction and college football pick for Saturday, November 7. Kentucky vs. Tennessee Pick: Tennessee ML (-225) My Tennessee vs. Kentucky best bet is on the Volunteers to win outright. Find the best line available on our live NCAAF odds page , and be sure to download the Action Network app for more picks and analysis. Kentucky vs Tennessee Odds, Betting Line, Point Spread Kentucky vs Tennessee Spread : Kentucky +6, Tennessee -6 Kentucky vs Tennessee Over/Under : 49.5 Total Points Kentucky vs Tennessee Moneyline : Kentucky ML +170, Tennessee ML -205 In one of the bigger surprises of this college football season, the Wildcats have emerged as one of the best teams in the entire country in head coach Will Stein's first year at the helm. Kentucky senior QB Kenny Minchey has been phenomenal in his first season in Lexington after spending three years at Notre Dame and throwing the ball only 30 times there. Minchey has thrown for 1755 yards and 14 touchdowns over the Wildcats' first eight games this season with just one turnover. Freshman WR Kenny Darby has been Minchey's favorite target with over 500 yards and three touchdowns. Stein's rushing attack has been effective too, with senior tailback CJ Baxter rushing for nearly 500 yards and eight touchdowns. The Wildcat offense is averaging just shy of 33 points per game this season, but will get its most difficult test on Saturday against an elite Tennessee pass rush. Kentucky's defense has thrived under defensive coordinator Jay Bateman, who has built an aggressive, havoc -creating unit that has fared well against some elite SEC offenses this season. The Wildcats lead the SEC in interceptions and pass breakups, boasting an elite secondary led by veteran safeties Ty Bryant and Jordan Castell. While its front seven struggled early this season, Kentucky has improved drastically in the trenches over the course of the season. The 8th-ranked Wildcats are in a great spot to potentially qualify for the playoffs, but still must face several difficult conference opponents, starting with the Vols in Week 10. The 16th-ranked Volunteers put their postseason hopes on the line as Josh Heupel's bunch looks to evade a third loss this season that would very likely ruin their playoff resume. After a very promising 6-1 start to the season despite an ongoing QB battle between George MacIntyre and Faizon Brandon , Tennessee was defeated on the road at South Carolina this past weekend for the Vols' second loss of the year. Now they face a must-win game, with lingering questions about whether Heupel will stick with MacIntyre under center or return to top-ranked freshman QB Brandon. Regardless, betting markets have made their stance quite clear, with Tennessee currently listed as a near-touchdown favorite despite the Wildcats' breakout 7-1 campaign. While WR Mike Matthews has recorded over 500 receiving yards this season, Tennessee has relied far more on its rushing attack, with tailback DeSean Bishop rushing for 957 yards and 11 touchdowns, ranking sixth and ninth in all of college football, respectively. However, the Vols' defense has thrived all year, particularly at home, where it allows SEC opponents the third-fewest PPG in the conference (16.25). Jim Knowles was brought in as defensive coordinator this past offseason after serving in the same capacity for Penn State , and has significantly improved a unit that fell to 81st in the country in EPA (Expected Points Added) last season. Tennessee's defense boasts an elite linebacker corps ranked in the top 10 nationally, featuring Edwin Spillman, Amare Campbell, Arion Carter, and Jeremiah Telander. While the Vols' defense has carried this team for most of the season, especially at home in Knoxville, their offense will need to show up in this matchup, given how impressive Michey has been at avoiding turnovers. I expect this to be one of the best matchups in an absolutely loaded Week 10 slate. While I have been very impressed with the Wildcats offense and a much-improved defensive unit, I expect the atmosphere to be quite chaotic given how difficult it is for SEC foes to escape Neyland Stadium in Knoxville with an outright victory. The Vols boast an extremely dominant pass rush that should give Kentucky's offensive line fits considering how much that unit has struggled to contain elite edge pressure. That said, I feel betting markets are giving Tennessee a tad too much credit given their fragile situation at QB. In what I expect to be a pretty closely contested matchup, I'm going with the Volunteers moneyline. I got it at -210 earlier this week as soon as the line opened, and while I typically don't lay that much juice on a moneyline, especially considering the volatility of betting college football, I have confidence Tennessee gets the outright win, but laying close to a touchdown versus a red-hot Wildcat bunch is far from ideal. Though Tennessee's moneyline has since crept up to -230, I still don't mind playing the Vols at that number. Pick: Tennessee ML (-225) Check out the latest college football odds updates in VegasInsider's most recent report !

Kentucky (7-1, 5-1) is also coming off of an open date and has a clear path to the SEC Championship Game and the CFP. Kentucky leads the league in turnover margin and fewest penalties. But UT can take control of this game by winning the line of scrimmage. That means DeSean Bishop earns bruising yards and UT's defensive line collapses the pocket around Kenny Minchey. Give Tennessee the edge because of the overwhelming atmosphere of Neyland Stadium in a night game in dark mode. Emmett Siegel, UT beat reporter: Tennessee 24, Kentucky 20 The Vols still have to find something in their passing game , which is statistically the worst in the SEC. Even if that doesn't come to fruition, though, Tennessee's rushing attack and defense have been good enough to beat the toughest teams on its schedule. Perhaps the open week helped Tennessee clean up some of last game's mistakes before playing a team that doesn't make many. Playing at home could push it over the top. Cora Hall, UT beat reporter: Kentucky 27, Tennessee 24 Both teams are had a week off and are rested going into this matchup, and the Wildcats have proven they can will their way to a win when it matters. The Vols will get close, but they've been too inconsistent to bet on a win here. Stephen Thompson, UT beat reporter: Tennessee 17, Kentucky 13 I've surrendered to the idea that George MacIntyre is who he is, at least for now. But Tennessee's defense is as good as any in the country and the Neyland effect will be a difference maker in another ugly, but tight win for the Vols. Wynton Jackson, sports reporter: Tennessee 26, Kentucky 21 The Vols likely need to be perfect throughout the rest of the season to reach the College Football Playoff. Coming off the bye, that road starts with an unexpected matchup against No. 7 Kentucky. The Wildcats have solid wins, but a trip to Neyland with a national spotlight brings heightened pressure. John Adams, columnist: Tennessee 27, Kentucky 20 The Wildcats have a better record and a higher national ranking than the Vols. Moreover, Kentucky is clearly headed in the right direction under first-year coach Will Stein. But history tells us that Tennessee is always the wrong direction for Kentucky football, which has lost 38 of the previous 41 games in the series. Gentry Estes, Tennessean columnist: Tennessee 23, Kentucky 14 Props to the Wildcats on a great season, but it just feels like they are due for a letdown in a tough rivalry road game. ET on Saturday night. This is a massive game with a lot at stake for both teams, the Wildcats are undefeated on the road this season and they will try to continue that streak in this game. We laid out the path to victory for Kentucky and the key areas they need to win to improve to 8-1 on the season. It is time to give some final thoughts on the matchup and give a game prediction. As I stated earlier in the week on my Tennessee defense preview , but I truly think this game comes down to Will Stein's offense versus Jim Knowles' defense. They have met three times and Coach Stein has gotten the best of Knowles in two of those three meetings. Kentucky has to continue to play efficient on offense and play clean. I think they have a great opportunity to methodically move the football down the field as they have all season against this defense. This game starts and ends in the trenches, on both sides of the football. Tennessee's defensive line is the strength of their team, but Kentucky's offensive line is playing better than any offensive line in the country. They have to stabilize defensive tackle Xavier Gilliam, who has been wrecking offensive gameplans all season long. A key matchup to watch is Kentucky center Coleton Price against Gilliam, Price has been one of the best centers in the country and he will have his hands full in this game. Kentucky has to win this game on the line of scrimmage, and I have confidence in the Wildcats offensive line to gain the edge in that matchup. Tennessee's offensive line has been above average as run blockers, but they do struggle in pass protection. Kentucky forcing Tennessee into a dropback heavy game script could be critical, but they have to stop the run in order to do that. Kentucky's defensive line has gotten consistent pressure all season, and I am very intrigued to see how this defensive line gets after a pocket passer like George MacIntyre because they have faced a mobile quarterback in every game this season. Kentucky has to win the line of scrimmage, and this is the best offensive line the Vols have faced this season. I think the Wildcats defensive line has been underrated this year, and they can make a statement on Saturday. The run defense has improved tremendously in the month of October, and slowing down the Vols heavy rushing attack is crucial. If they can force Tennessee into a heavy dropback game, Kentucky will be able to create turnovers like they have all season. Truthfully, I believe the biggest advantage is Kentucky's coaching staff getting two weeks to prepare for this football game. Tennessee is coming off the bye week as well, but Josh Heupel and Jim Knowles are going to do what they do. Kentucky's coaching staff has added plenty of wrinkles week-to-week, so I can only imagine what they will have in store with two weeks to prepare. This is an advantage for Kentucky, particularly on the offensive side of the football. We all know this history of this series, it has not been kind to Kentucky. However, this is a different era of college football and Kentucky football. If you remove the history and helmet logos, I think Kentucky has the advantage at quarterback and offensive line as well as a hotshot head coach that has done an unthinkable turnaround in year one for this program. It will be a close game in the fourth quarter, and how could you not trust Will Stein and Kenny Minchey under those circumstances. Prediction: Kentucky 24, Tennessee 20 This article originally appeared on UK Wildcats Wire: Kentucky at Tennessee: Final thoughts and prediction

home.headline: Tennessee vs. Texas A&M initial availability report
home.blurb: Wednesday night, the SEC released the initial availability report. Weathersby joins six players already out for the season. Texas A&M lists offensive lineman Trovon Baugh as doubtful and wide receiver Mario Craver as questionable. Craver is the Aggies’ second-leading receiver with 311 yards and three touchdowns. Below is the full availability report for Texas A&M. Saturday, No. 8 Tennessee will take on Texas A&M on the road in College Station, Texas. The Vols are coming off their big win over the Kentucky Wildcats last Saturday. In that game, edge rusher Tyree Weathersby went down with a season-ending knee injury. Tennessee had stayed fairly healthy for a while after the first few weeks of the season. Weathersby was having an amazing season as the sacks leader on the team and third in the Southeastern Conference with seven. Weathersby also had 20 tackles, two fumble recoveries and even a pass deflection this season. “I hate it for Tyree,” head coach Josh Heupel said Monday. “He’s played extremely well. He’s worked extremely hard. He was playing his best football. And I know he’ll bounce back from it, but obviously a huge bump in the road for him.” During Saturday’s win, tight end DaSaahn Brame exited the game after failing to maintain control of a pass in the end zone, according to the officials. Brame’s head hit the ground hard, and he was eventually helped off the field. He is not on the report, and Heupel said on Monday’s “Mike Keith Show” that he should be good to go. Heupel also spoke to the incomplete call. “DaSaahn’s doing good. We feel like he’ll be in a great spot for game day. When I was talking with the officials, we hadn’t gotten the report back postgame yet. That typically happens in the middle of the week. “But at the end of the day, he didn’t come down with the football, didn’t maintain control of it when he was on the ground. So that was the ruling that they gave me, and they said that they did review it up top as well.” No. 8 Tennessee and Texas A&M will kick off at 3 p.m. ET Saturday at Kyle Field in College Station, Texas. The game will be televised on ESPN. The Vols will try for their first win at Kyle Field after losing in double-overtime, 45-38, during their only other visit there back in 2016. home.headline: Texas A&M WR Mario Craver Faces Injury Uncertainty Ahead of Tennessee Game
home.blurb: Texas A&M’s 2026 season hasn’t gone according to plan. What began with College Football Playoff aspirations has turned into a fight for bowl eligibility, and the Aggies are running out of opportunities to salvage something from a disappointing year. Texas A&M listed just five players, with wide receiver Mario Craver the only one designated as questionable. That’s a welcome change from some of the longer injury reports the Aggies have dealt with this season, although it doesn’t mean everybody is ready to play. Offensive lineman Trovon Baugh is doubtful, while wide receivers Terry Bussey and Kelshaun Johnson remain out. Offensive lineman Blake Ivy is also ruled out. Those absences aren’t new — all are out for the remainder of the season — but they continue to limit the options available to Elko down the stretch run of the season. Six other Tennessee players are out, including tight end Ethan Davis, wide receiver Joakim Dodson, offensive lineman Wendell Moe Jr., linebacker Jaedon Harmon and defensive backs Edrees Farooq and Dylan Lewis. Mike Elko’s team enters Saturday’s matchup against Tennessee with a 4-5 record, needing two wins over its final three games to qualify for a bowl. At least Wednesday’s initial SEC availability report gave the Aggies something encouraging to consider. Texas A&M Injury Report vs. Tennessee Craver has appeared on the report repeatedly throughout the year but has still been able to dress and take the field once the game arrived. He played against South Carolina, so his latest designation isn’t necessarily cause for panic. Still, his availability matters for a Texas A&M offense that needs capable wide receivers in order to move the football. Tennessee has more names on its report, most notably defensive lineman Tyree Weathersby , who suffered a season-ending injury against Kentucky this past weekend. Weathersby is one of the best pass rushers in the country, and his absence will be sorely missed by a Volunteers defense that’s been terrorizing opposing offenses all season. Texas A&M has lost five of its last six games against SEC competition, including a frustrating 17-9 defeat at the hands of South Carolina last weekend. A loss to Tennessee wouldn’t mathematically eliminate the Aggies from bowl contention, but it would leave them needing wins over Oklahoma and Texas to finish the regular season. Texas A&M hosts No. 8 Tennessee at 2 p.m. CT Saturday at Kyle Field. The game will be televised on ESPN. picks.blurb: Colin Cowherd Predicts National Championship Rematch After Notre Dame Win Over Miami Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS Fox Sports host Colin Cowherd is sticking with Notre Dame and Miami as his national championship pairing after the Fighting Irish handed the top-ranked Hurricanes their first loss of the season, 31-24, Saturday night in South Bend. “Nothing I saw last night changes that opinion ,” Cowherd wrote on X on Sunday morning, adding that he said before the season the two programs “would meet for the natty” and that “only Georgia is close.” Why is Cowherd still riding with Notre Dame? Fans are seen on the field after Notre Dame Fighting Irish defeated the Miami Hurricanes | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Cowherd backed the Irish before they played a snap. “I picked Notre Dame to win the whole thing. They’re going to be my national champion ,” he said in late August. Cowherd backed the Irish before they played a snap. “I picked Notre Dame to win the whole thing. They’re going to be my national champion ,” he said in late August. Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr held up his end of that pick Saturday, completing 29 of 40 passes for 319 yards and three touchdowns. He hit Micah Gilbert for two scores and Jordan Faison for another as the Irish built a 24-3 lead early in the third quarter. Miami pulled within a touchdown, but Notre Dame safety Luke Talich intercepted Miami quarterback Darian Mensah late in the third quarter and later broke up a potential tying touchdown pass to tight end Elija Lofton. The win mattered most for an Irish team that entered with the No. 11 College Football Playoff ranking that surprised ESPN’s Kirk Herbstreit. Notre Dame head coach Marcus Freeman called it “ as special of a moment , as special of an outcome that I’ve been a part of since I’ve been the head coach here.” The Irish close the regular season against Boston College, SMU and Syracuse. Malachi Toney and a Miami rematch Miami (FL) Hurricanes wide receiver Malachi Toney (1) celebrates with tight end Gavin Mueller (87) after scoring a touchdown | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Cowherd attached one condition to his title game pick. “I would take the Canes in a rematch if Malachi Toney plays,” he wrote. Cowherd attached one condition to his title game pick. “I would take the Canes in a rematch if Malachi Toney plays,” he wrote. Miami wide receiver Malachi Toney suffered a high-ankle sprain in practice Wednesday and had tightrope surgery Thursday. The sophomore led the ACC with 73 catches, 1,027 receiving yards and 13 touchdowns through eight games, and CBS Sports reported he’s expected to miss four to six weeks . That timeline could put Toney back for the ACC Championship Game on Dec. 5 and keeps him on track for the playoff. His absence showed in a first half that ended with Miami trailing 17-3. Mensah then threw three second-half touchdown passes, two of them to Duke transfer Cooper Barkate. Miami finishes the regular season with home games against Duke, Virginia Tech and Boston College. Georgia rolls Ole Miss in Oxford Georgia Bulldogs head coach Kirby Smart reacts during the second half against the Mississippi Rebels | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The second-ranked Bulldogs backed up Cowherd’s lone exception Saturday, routing Ole Miss 42-7 as Georgia quarterback Gunner Stockton threw four touchdown passes and ran for another. The second-ranked Bulldogs backed up Cowherd’s lone exception Saturday, routing Ole Miss 42-7 as Georgia quarterback Gunner Stockton threw four touchdown passes and ran for another. Georgia led 28-0 at halftime, rushed for 295 yards and snapped Ole Miss’ 16-game home winning streak . The win was Georgia head coach Kirby Smart’s first at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, and it came days after former Ohio State head coach Urban Meyer named Georgia the best team in college football . The selection committee releases its second College Football Playoff rankings Tuesday at approximately 9 p.m. ET on ESPN, and Georgia has a strong case to replace Miami at No. 1. My Miami vs. Notre Dame prediction and college football picks back Darian Mensah to keep things close without his top target, Malachi Toney. The Fighting Irish are 7.5-point home favorites as Miami visits Notre Dame Stadium in Notre Dame, Ind., on Saturday, Nov. 7. Kickoff is set for 7:30 p.m. ET on NBC, with College GameDay also in town. Miami vs Notre Dame predictions for Week 10 ⭐Spread prediction Over/Under prediction Prop prediction Miami TT Over 23.5 TOP PICK Who will win Miami vs Notre Dame today: Miami +7.5 The news that Malachi Toney was injured in practice this week and won't play against Notre Dame has dominated headlines and shifted the Fighting Irish from 5.5-point favorites to 7.5-point favorites. But even without Toney, I like Miami to cover +6.5 or better on the road. Darian Mensah is among the Heisman Trophy favorites for a reason; he leads the country in QBR (90.3) and adjusted completion percentage (86.2%). He also has one of the best running back duos in college football and a No. 2 wide receiver in Cooper Barkate , whom he trusts immensely. Mensah won the ACC Championship at Duke last year with Barkate as his top receiver (1,106 receiving yards). Even without Toney, Miami has more talented playmakers than CJ Carr and Notre Dame, and the Irish aren't healthy in their back seven. Notre Dame has ruled out linebacker Drayk Bowen, safety Tae Johnson, and cornerback DJ McKinney. Miami vs Notre Dame Over/Under pick: Over 54.5 With Mensah and Carr arguably the top two QBs in college football this season, I would play the Over at 55.5 or better , even with Toney out. Mensah is deadly accurate and ranks No. 1 in college football in TD passes (25), with Miami ranking No. 2 in the country in offensive success rate (52.4%). Notre Dame isn't far behind, though, sitting No. 4 in offensive success rate (51.4%) thanks to Carr, who r anks eighth in QBR (82.6), 11th in big-time throw rate (6.9%), and 18th in TD passes (18). Miami's pass defense has also been suspect at times, and Carr can take advantage. The Hurricanes are ranked just 110th in EPA per dropback. In the Fighting Irish's previous two games against teams ranked in the Top 50 by SP+ , they hit the Over. Miami vs Notre Dame prop: Miami TT Over 23.5 Toney is one of the best wide receivers in recent college football history, but Miami's offense has been a force with Mensah at QB and Dawson calling plays, and I don't think it will just collapse without its top receiver. I like the Hurricanes to hit the Over on their team total at 23.5 or better against a Notre Dame defense that allowed 28 points to BYU without its best offensive player, LJ Martin . Miami's passing attack is far more prolific than BYU's, with Miami's offense leading the country in EPA per dropback and net adjusted EPA per play. Notre Dame's defense has also been shaky on money downs this season, ranking 67th nationally in third/fourth down success rate (43.6%). Miami vs Notre Dame combo This is the "game of the century" of the week in college football and the No. 1 must-watch matchup in my Week 10 Top 25 predictions , featuring the season's most loaded slate. While Miami would certainly be an upset threat to Notre Dame with Toney, I don't think Mario Cristobal's team will roll over in its biggest game of the season. The Hurricanes ended last season by covering the spread in four straight College Football Playoff games , including three as an underdog. Cristobal knows how to get his team up, and Notre Dame has had slow starts in three of its last four games, failing to cover in all three of those games as a favorite . Sep 19, 2026; South Bend, Indiana, USA; Notre Dame Fighting Irish quarterback CJ Carr (13) looks on after the game against the Michigan State Spartans at Notre Dame Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Nick Shepkowski · Notre Dame Fighting Irish On SI Fri, November 6, 2026 at 4:28 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads For the first time in exactly seven years, Notre Dame welcomes the No. 1 team in the nation to South Bend. Like last time, when top-ranked an unbeaten Clemson came to town late in the 2020 season, another ACC foe brings an unbeaten an No. 1 ranking. This time its the mighty Miami Hurricanes and the rivalry between the two programs is as strong as ever. So does Notre Dame knock off No. 1? Or does Miami leave South Bend with the No. 1 overall seed in the College Football Playoff seemingly on ice? Here's what the matchups favor on Saturday night in South Bend: When Miami Has the Ball Malachi Toney or not , this Miami offense is like few in all of college football. Sure, its biggest playmaker is out, but can Notre Dame slow down the thunder and lightning running attack of Javian Mallory and Mark Fletcher? Furthermore, Darian Mensah has 25 touchdown passes to just one interception all season long. Can Notre Dame's defense, which will be playing a bit shorthanded itself, keep Miami in check enough? That has been a major issue in the biggest games over the last two seasons. Advantage: Miami When Notre Dame Has the Ball Notre Dame has one of the better offensive lines in college football but has its work cut out against this Miami defensive front. The Hurricanes are allowing just 2.4 yards per rush attempt this year, which means Notre Dame likely won't be able to play the same ball possession type game it likes to. That means CJ Carr's moment is now: Miami has a pass defense that has surrendered huge numbers in narrow escapes against both Florida State and North Carolina. Can Carr do enough to win what could very possibly turn into a track meet between the powerhouse programs? Advantage: Notre Dame Special Teams For the Win? So far we're pretty much at a toss-up, and we figure special teams will end up being huge. Notre Dame doesn't have to have a kick return for a touchdown to win this thing, but overall, its numbers in kick return, punt return, kick coverage, and punt coverage give the Irish an advantage statisically. Factor in a veteran kicker in Spencer Porath who is Notre Dame's best at the position in years and special teams coordinator Marty Biagi, who has had a bit of a quiet year by his standards, to date, and I expect to see the Irish steal a possession and deciding score as a result. Nick Shepkowski's Prediction: Saturday night ends with CJ Carr suddenly being the Heisman Trophy front runner after he throws for 350 yards, four touchdowns, and leads a late drive that ends with a Notre Dame field goal as time expires. picks.blurb: The Anti-Preview: No. 4 Notre Dame Fighting Irish VS No. 1 Miami Hurricanes - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NFL news, live updates Misiorowski, Schlittler win Cy Youngs NFL midseason awards Rex Ryan arrested Skubal suitors emerge The Anti-Preview: No. 4 Notre Dame Fighting Irish VS No. 1 Miami Hurricanes Joshua Vowles · SB Nation Fri, November 6, 2026 at 8:08 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Are you ready for this — like really ready for this? The No. 1 ranked Miami Hurricanes are in town to play the No. 4 ranked Notre Dame Fighting Irish, and the stakes are about as high as they get for ND. If the Irish lose, the season is basically over — even with three regular season games left on the schedule. If Notre Dame wins… the path to the playoff and a first round bye is illuminated. With no USC on the schedule this year, having an old rival like Miami being in this position only makes things even grander than all of the hype and hoopla a top 4 matchup brings with College Gameday in attendance. This is a GIANT of a game, and you have to be ready for it. While I absolutely prefer the Gulf of Mexico side of Florida, I do appreciate the flavors and culture of Miami — but I also love mashups. No one can tell me this ISN'T perfect tailgating food — because it is. Insanely delicious and completely mobile with its delivery system… The Cubano. BYU VS Utah — NOON Alabama VS LSU — 3:30 PM Georgia VS Ole Miss — 7:30 PM Of course, the games only matter if Notre Dame wins, but the outcomes should have a massive impact on the CFP rankings — as well as the narrative SEC spinners want to send out. Before the Malachi Toney injury news came out, I was riding with a 30-23 prediction with Notre Dame on the right side of things. Now… things have changed. Toney isn't just the best WR on Miami's team, he's one of the best players in the country — period. He's so good, that when he's not in the game, Miami's "potent offense" goes to shit — and Darian Mensah looks like a Duke QB and not the QB of the No.1 ranked Canes. Notre Dame is backed into a corner, and I believe that will create the sense of urgency needed to come out and dominate the game early, and then ride out a win late. Notre Dame 34, Miami 20

This is the ND offense preview for the week. The 'Canes are 5th overall in SP+ while ND is 3rd . The Irish kicking game is 17th while UM's is ranked 19th . Per ESPN , ND has a 61.3 % win expectancy as 4.5 point favorites at home. The Irish are 3rd in FBS in scoring offense putting up 40.4 PPG which is 2nd to only Miami and North Texas. The ND offense is 2nd in SP+ offense behind only the Miami Hurricanes. The high scoring Irish offense will be up against Miami's defense which is 23rd now in SP+ after the UNC game. The 'Canes are 25th in scoring allowed while giving up 19.3 PPG. The Irish are 36th in FBS in 3rd down conversion offense, picking up the 1st 43 % of the time. On 4th down ND is 16th in FBS picking up the 1st 74 % of the time. Miami's 3rd down defense is 95th in FBS allowing opponents to move the sticks 42 % of the time. ND's turnover margin per game is 3rd in FBS at +1.8 while Miami is 9th at +1.0 TOMPG. For obvious reasons I'm looking at ND's lone loss to BYU and their win over UNC. ND lost to BYU 28-24 and beat UNC 37-26 . Against UNC the Irish offense finished 7-of-16 on money downs with zero turnovers. CJ Carr averaged 8.1 yards per pass attempt with five total TD's against the Tar Heels. The Irish averaged 5.4 yards per carry while Jordan Faison caught two TD's on 16.5 yards per catch. UNC finished with zero sacks, two TFL's and five PBU's versus the Irish offense. Above- Splitting two lost safeties with a deep post… gives me some nervous vibes here re the ND receivers and CJ Carr carving up the Miami safety room with a deep shot. Above- More abuse on safety types with a slot fade. One of my favorite passing concepts. If he's even, he's leavin' and he'll head to the front pylon here. Above- ND ran a little wide zone, the RB bounces this one outside and takes advantage of the UNC DB's in the open field. Miami is really struggling in the open field without Keionte Scott. Above- UNC gets caught here with both DB's to that side being aggressive and playing down on the short throw. Miami is more likely to have both on the deep shot and no one short. I don't see this being as much of an issue with the 'Canes in country cover 3. Above- The check down to the RB's in the middle of the field is a Miami weakness. Toure and Smith need to play tighter coverage and rally to help each other at the ball. Above- Keep CJ Carr inside. Here UNC plays an outside contain on QB sweep and it forces Carr inside for a loss. Staying on that outside hip is key. Above- ND can fight for the tough yards. Here they pick up 4th and 2 on the inside and in a me vs you rep ND's RB wins. Above- An explosive TFL from an edge guy squeeze and chasing from the back side? I like Marquise Lightfoot here for this type of havoc play. Let him chase this down and not drop into the flats, please. Above- The UNC player has to fight to get outside of CJ Carr's right hip. If he can get out there he can box the Q back to his help. Instead Carr gets outside and scrambles for a TD. He can and will run vs. Miami's slow LB's. Above- An open field shot with the sideline there for help… and it's missed? Looks really familiar to me from the Miami defense. Miami has to clean up open field angles and tackling vs. ND. Against BYU the Irish offense finished 12-of-23 on money downs with one turnover. Carr averaged only 5.3 yards per attempt with zero TD's and a lost fumble. The Cougars didn't sack Carr but picked up three TFL's and seven PBU's. Jaden Greathouse led the way for ND with 15.6 yards per catch while the rushing attack was held to 3.8 yards per carry but had two scores. Above- James is going to be a tough one to take down. He had BYU lunging all over the place as he juked and cut for 4.8 yards per carry vs. a top-25 SP+ defense. Above- How do you blow up counter? BYU doesn't wrong arm it but they do control the edge, they also get interior penetration. This is a MUST HAVE game from Moten and Scott at DT. Above- Even in blanket coverage ND has been getting work from Faison, Greathouse and Bettis Jr. on the outside to name a few. That's hardly Miami's flaccid zone. Above- James with another shifty carry. He's a one-cut-and-go back like Mallory. Above- The ND OL dominated BYU's front 6 here and gave the back two ways to go in the red zone. He used his eyes, saw where the safety wasn't, and scored. Above- CJ Carr has aded the dreaded back shoulder throw to his repertoire and the ND WR's can get a little fyzical. That's not great, Bob, for a CB crew that looks baby dookie soft. Above- Carr has always been a solid scrambler, he's really improved at that skill this season. He scrambled around to find a wide open target here and Miami can't let WR's get behind them on scramble drill plays. Above- This is where Smith and Toure should excel, except teams have baited them inside and thrown some RPO's that have them stick. Damned if you do, damned if you don't. It's why a lot of LB coaches are now using a squat technique where the LB doesn't take 2-read steps forward, instead he hits a quick baby squat to force the run on 2nd level RPO's. Above- Hetherman has cut Toure off at what he does best- run blitz. Where are those TFL run throughs from a year ago? Get the AARPLB out of pass drops and let him blitz. Above- Pretty crazy not to call DPI on this slot fade but ND did get away with the throw-by on the back shoulder throw earlier. Just a tough call (also this was another clock disaster, right?) for the win. The Canyonero Keys to Victory main theme from the summer was that Miami needs to win bully ball vs. Notre Dame. I'm not so sure if that's true now after the season has unfolded the way it has. Miami may now have to win a shoot out vs. ND and CJ Carr. The 'Canes pass defense is horrendous and ND clearly saw the UNC game on film and will try to attack the outside with WR's vs Safeties and the inside with TE's deep up the seam. Miami needs to improve their tackling, and coverage when it comes to the safety position. The LB's are a lost cause in space. Miami will continue to see screens, seams, digs, and outs until the CB's prove they'll tackle, and the LB/S prove they'll cover. We'll get to the individual keys in the ND Defense preview that's out Friday at 8am.

Above- I love this Glance route inside stuff to Toney on the RPO tag. Mensah has to throw these low and inside closer to the end line or front pylons. Who can replace him with that route running ability? Maybe Barkate? The Canyonero Keys to Victory main theme from the summer was that Miami needs to win bully ball vs. Notre Dame. picks.blurb: The nation's No. 1 scoring offense still offers plenty of ways to attack even the No. 5 Notre Dame defense, which has surrendered 14 or more points just twice en route to a 7-1 start. Darian Mensah remains a Heisman Trophy favorite who's got a 25:1 touchdown-to-interception ratio. Mark Fletcher Jr. and Javian Mallory have formed a potent power-running game that's averaging more than 202 yards per game (the Irish gave up 4 yards per carry and two TDs in their lone loss to BYU, then surrendered 212 last week to Navy in a game that was tight in the first half). But keeping up with a home team motivated by unbridled vengeance will be a challenge given the way Miami's defense has played recently. Top cornerback O.J. Frederique is still on the shelf, and the secondary has been torched to the tune of 341 yards by North Carolina's Billy Edwards , 334 yards by Pitt's backup quarterback and four touchdowns by Florida State's Ashton Daniels , more dangerous as a runner than a passer. That's especially bad news as Miami (8-0, 6-0 in ACC) now gets C.J. Carr, who's built his own Heisman case with 1,849 passing yards and 18 TDs against just one pick. The Canes' strength has been their top-ranked run defense (60.8 yards per game), which could help in making the Irish one-dimensional. As long as that one dimension can hold up, that is. away.headline: Malachi Toney's injury, explained: Doctor outlines Miami WR's return timeline and 2026 outlook
away.blurb: Per the school, Toney will undergo surgery to repair the sprain, which will put him out for at least the remainder of Miami's regular season. According to On3Sports, Toney will undergo what's called a Tightrope surgery to repair the sprain. The typical recovery timetable for the surgery is around four weeks. In 2019, Tagovailoa suffered the injury again on his opposite ankle, which he had injured the season before, during No. 1 Alabama's 35-13 win over Tennessee on Oct. 19. Initially, then-Tide head coach Nick Saban had said he would be out for one to two weeks with an ankle sprain. So theoretically, Toney could return in time for Miami's ACC title game in four weeks, assuming the Hurricanes make it. That may also depend on if Miami truly needs to win that game to make it into the CFP. But a return to the team in time for a CFP game in six weeks perhaps is the more conservative approach. The No. 1 Miami Hurricanes ' College Football Playoff hopes took a massive hit this week. The Canes' star wide receiver Malachi Toney suffered a high ankle sprain in practice ahead of Miami's massive road game against No. 11 Notre Dame on Saturday night. As of Nov. 6, there are six weeks until the first round of the first round of the College Football Playoff. That's all to say things are gonna be tight. The Sporting News spoke with Dr. Norman E. Waldrop III, a foot and ankle surgeon at the Andrews Sports Medicine & Orthopedic Center, a world-renowned orthopedic clinic in Birmingham, Ala. Dr. Waldrop, who specializes in athlete injuries, is also on staff with the Alabama Crimson Tide football team and New Orleans Saints. Below, Dr. Waldrop explains Toney's diagnosis, what his surgery will entail and what the recovery process typically looks like. MORE: How villainous Miami ruled the 1980s and steered its rivalry with Notre Dame What to know about Miami WR Malachi Toney's diagnosis and recovery What happened to Malachi Toney? As first reported by ESPN's Pete Thamel , Toney suffered a high ankle sprain during practice on Wednesday ahead of the Notre Dame game. Miami issued a statement that Toney was "undergoing further testing." Shortly thereafter, Thamel confirmed the star RB was having surgery. Toney's injury occurred during practice on Wednesday when he got "caught up in a play with a cornerback", according to On3's Pete Nakos . What is Malachi Toney's injury? According to reports, Toney suffered a high ankle sprain during practice on Wednesday ahead of the Notre Dame game. "There are different grades [of sprains]," Dr. Waldrop told The Sporting News. "You have grade one, grade two, to grade three. Grade twos are the ones that are the gray area. Grade ones are stable, and you can play through them. It can be as quick as a week. It can sometimes be two or three weeks. Grade twos are the gray area where it's what we call 'subtle instability,' and that's where it gets difficult in terms of whether a player can play or not play." MORE: Nine things you may have forgo
