away.blurb: The Miami Hurricanes shared a new development on star wide receiver Malachi Toney as he recovers from the ankle injury that sidelined him for Saturday’s Notre Dame Fighting Irish game. Miami shared the news on X, announcing that Toney and quarterback Darian Mensah have been named semifinalists for the 2026 Walter Camp Player of the Year Award . “The Miami dynamic duo,” the Hurricanes posted on X . “Malachi Toney and Darian Mensah have been named semifinalists for the Walter Camp Player of the Year Award 🙌” Toney is one of two wide receivers among the 20 semifinalists, joining Ohio State star Jeremiah Smith. Mensah, meanwhile, is one of nine quarterbacks contending for the award heading into Week 11. This national honor comes less than a week after Toney underwent surgery for a high ankle sprain suffered in practice. Reports placed his expected recovery timeline at four to six weeks, meaning Miami could get him back later in the season and in time for the College Football Playoffs. Before the injury, Toney had established himself as one of college football’s most productive receivers. He has 73 receptions for 1,027 yards and 13 touchdowns through eight games, ranking among the national leaders in each category. Toney’s absence was immediately felt last weekend as Miami suffered its first loss of the season, falling 31-24 to Notre Dame without its top receiver. Mensah, meanwhile, made the Walter Camp semifinalist list after emerging as one of the nation’s top quarterbacks in his first, and likely last , season with Miami. He has completed 212 of 276 (76.8%) passes for 2,694 yards and 25 touchdowns against just two interceptions. The Walter Camp Player of the Year has been awarded since 1967 and is voted on by the 138 FBS head coaches and sports information directors. Five finalists will be announced later this month, with the winner revealed Dec. 11 during the ESPN College Football Awards Show. Miami dropped to No. 7 in the latest CFP committee rankings, with the Hurricanes hosting Duke on Saturday. The Bulldogs came back from a nine-point fourth-quarter deficit in the first meeting, outscoring the Rebels 17-0 in the fourth to win 43-35, but Ole Miss would have its revenge. It was in the College Football Playoff quarterfinal at the Sugar Bowl that the Rebels ended Georgia's season with a 39-34 win thanks largely to the heroics of quarterback Trinidad Chambliss . So what will these two deliver this year? While plenty has changed from last year's teams to this year, both quarterbacks return, and there are high stakes involved here. Georgia debuted at No. 2 in the first College Football Playoff rankings of the season, and a win here would solidify their chances of reaching the SEC Championship. On the other side, the Rebels need a win to gain firmer ground. They're No. 10 in the rankings, putting them on the precipice of losing an at-large bid. Plus, a loss here would be their third in SEC play, essentially ending their conference title hopes, and putting them in a position where they need to win out and hope for some other teams to lose to return to the playoff . Georgia vs. Ole Miss: Need to know This is the fifth straight time these two have met while ranked: Maybe that doesn't seem like something that's all that impressive to you, but for context, it had happened only five times in the first 46 meetings between the schools. Georgia has had the better end of most meetings, as they lead the series 34-14-1, and a win for Ole Miss this weekend would give the Rebels consecutive wins over the Dawgs for the first time since the 1995 and 1996 seasons. Kirby Smart has done well against ranked opponents: The Georgia coach is 44-18 against AP-ranked teams during his tenure in Athens. That's the fifth-best record by any head coach against ranked teams in AP Poll history (minimum of 20 games). That includes a stretch of six wins in their last seven against ranked teams. The last loss? To Ole Miss in the playoff last year. Trinidad Chambliss could tie a school record here: Chambliss has thrown for at least one touchdown in 21 consecutive games. If he throws one against Georgia, it will put him in a tie with former Ole Miss QB Chad Kelly for most consecutive games with a TD pass at 22. Our Staff Picks and Final Scores Skip to main content SI.COM FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS No. 10 Ole Miss (6-2, 4-2) and No. 2 Georgia (7-1, 5-1) are set to square off on Saturday , in what will mark one of the biggest and most consequential games in the history of Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. In order to maintain control of its College Football Playoff destiny, Ole Miss will have to knock off Georgia for the third time in the program’s last four matchups. With a loss, the Rebels will put their season resume in the hands of the playoff committee with little optimism of returning to meaningful postseason play. Considering what Ole Miss has left in the final quarter of its season, there would be a lot of ground to make up. Ahead of the Rebels' top-10 matchup, Ole Miss On SI predicts which team wins and why. Ole Miss Rebels On SI Staff Predictions Oct 18, 2025; Athens, Georgia, USA; Georgia Bulldogs quarterback Gunner Stockton (14) runs the ball for a touchdown against Mississippi Rebels defensive tackle Will Echoles (52) during the first half of the game at Sanford Stadium. Trinidad Chambliss and the Rebels offense was unstoppable in both matchups, particularly in Round 2, when they knocked of the Bulldogs in the College Football Playoff. This year, the calculus has changed a bit. The Rebels have a new play caller, and new weapons on the outside. The Defense has also been struggling as of late. On the other side, the Bulldogs are built on defense, running the football and controlling the clock - exactly where Ole Miss has been exploited defensively. For Ole Miss to win here, I think Chambliss - especially without Kewan Lacy in the lineup - is going to have to be Superman. We have seen him do it before plenty of times, but if the Bulldogs can deploy a similar game plan that Texas did two weeks ago, it could be a long day. Shekai Mills-Knight could be an X-factor, but it's hard to be able to rely on a redshirt freshman on a stage like this. The Rebels do have an elite home field advantage, but at the end of the day, I think it all comes down to the Rebels defense and if they can hold up against the Georgia run game. I'll take the Dawgs in a tight one. Georgia 31, Ole Miss 27 Understandably, almost everyone had the LSU game circled on Ole Miss’ schedule going into the season. Offensively, Trinidad Chambliss will need to play a game similar to the one he played against LSU all the way back in Week 3. The version of Chambliss we saw against Auburn was the next closest thing, and he’ll have to continue adding yards with his legs even on plays that aren’t broken down. Without Kewan Lacy, Ole Miss will need efficiency from Chambliss, Makhi Frazier and Shekai Mills-Knight on the ground. The Rebels will also desperately need a bounce back game from one of its most explosive players in Deuce Alexander Ole Miss was in an eerily similar spot in November of the 2024 season. Like that weekend, I’m picking the Rebels to get the job done again against Georgia, but it should be much closer than the game that was last played in Oxford between these two. Ole Miss 34, Georgia 31 With the Rebels already having two losses this season, I think Saturday night’s game is a must-win to keep their playoff hopes strong. That should translate into a motivated team and an electric environment in Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, and when playing in The Vaught, especially at night, there isn’t a team in the country I’d take over Ole Miss. The Rebels are 26-1 at home since 2023, including a victory over the Bulldogs in the 2024 regular season that had very similar stakes as this game. Picking any team, let alone one that’s been as hot and cold as Ole Miss has been at times this season, to beat the No. 2 team in the country could age poorly. Despite that, give me Pete Golding, Trinidad Chambliss and the rest of the Ole Miss Rebels to win and keep their playoff and SEC Championship ambitions alive and send the Rebel fans home happy on Saturday night. Kirby Smart’s side will never go down easy, and Gunnar Stockton is a solid leader for the Bulldogs offense. Sparks will fly in Oxford, but a repeat of 2024 is in order. The 42-7 loss came at a terrible time for the Rebels, as much of their conference championship and playoff hopes were dashed. Georgia was the Rebels' third conference loss of the season, putting them sixth in the SEC standings and making them a long shot to reach the SEC championship game. For the playoffs, Ole Miss got its first sign of where it stands on Sunday when the AP Poll dropped the team from No. 12 to No. 19 . These two teams played twice last year. One game was in Athens and one was in the Sugar Bowl for a College Football Playoff quarterfinal game. Both were epic showdowns that involved second half comebacks. So that means that Kirby Smart and Pete Golding could be in for another back and forth game. These two teams feature some of the best players in the entire county. Georgia is favored, and advanced stats point this in Georgia’s favor, but Ole Miss has Trinidad Chambliss and the home crowd. Let’s make three bold predictions: Georgia Sacks Trinidad Chambliss at Least Three Times This is a different Georgia defense that Chambliss will be facing off against. Last year, the Dawgs managed just 20 sacks in 14 games. They are up to 26 this season in only eight games. Georgia didn’t take Chambliss down behind the line of scrimmage a single time in either matchup a season ago. Part of that was because of the magician-like escapability Chambliss showed off in new Orleans. This year is different for this defense and Chris Cole has leveled up to be one of the biggest difference makers on that side of the ball in all of college football. My Georgia vs. Ole Miss prediction and college football picks for tonight expect Kirby Smart's defense to rise to the occasion against Trinidad Chambliss & Co. as the Bulldogs seek revenge for last year's Sugar Bowl loss to the Rebels. Georgia is a 3.5-point favorite as it visits Vaught-Hemingway Stadium in Oxford, Miss., on Saturday, Nov. 7, while the total sits at 56.5. Don't miss kickoff at 7:30 p.m. ET on ABC. TOP PICK Who will win Georgia vs Ole Miss today: Georgia -3.5 Georgia and Ole Miss played two wild shootouts last year, with the Bulldogs winning the regular-season matchup and the Rebels taking it in the Sugar Bowl. This time around, I like Georgia to cover as many as 6.5 points on the road against Ole Miss. Defense will be the difference in the matchup this year, with Georgia having one of the best in the country ( ranked No. 2 by SP+ ), and Ole Miss' being one of the worst in the SEC. With the Rebels down All-American running back Kewan Lacy , the Bulldogs' defense can lock in on stopping Trinidad Chambliss . Chambliss has faced one other defense ranked top five by SP+, Texas , and struggled in a loss. Against the Longhorns, he threw three interceptions and put up a season-low 60% adjusted completion percentage. Georgia vs Ole Miss Over/Under pick: Under 56.5 Though both games between these teams last year were full of points, Georgia's defense should keep it relatively low-scoring this time around, and I would play the Under at 55.5 or better . The Bulldogs' defense ranks top 20 nationally in available yards percentage (33.5%) , havoc rate (19.4%), and success rate allowed (35.2%). With no Lacy for Ole Miss, it'll put even more on Chambliss, who has frequently had to carry the team this season, and we saw that approach fall flat against Texas. However, Georgia's offense hasn't been lighting up the scoreboard lately either, averaging just 23.6 points per game in its last three outings. So while this is one of the must-watch matchups in my Week 10 Top 25 predictions , it's not because I'm expecting another shootout. Georgia vs Ole Miss combo Ole Miss is a feast-or-famine type of team. The Rebels beat LSU and Missouri , but were blown out by Florida and fell behind so quickly against Texas that they couldn't dig themselves out. That's what happens when you lean so heavily on a star QB to make up for an inconsistent run game and one of the worst defenses in the SEC. Against Georgia, Chambliss won't be Superman; Smart has too much NFL talent on a defense that's allowed more than 20 points just once this season. If Ole Miss falls behind, Georgia's offense will lean on Gunner Stockton to manage the game and take a ball-control approach against a Rebels defense ranked 88th in the country in EPA per rush. Ole Miss team total Under 26.5 Georgia team total Over 30.5 Georgia vs Ole Miss prop: Ole Miss team total Under 26.5 Chambliss can only do so much, and against a freakishly athletic and long Georgia defense, I don't think Ole Miss will be scoring at nearly as high a clip as it has against lesser SEC teams. I would take the Under on Ole Miss' team total at 24.5 or better . Georgia linebacker Chris Cole is arguably the best defensive player in the country, and Glenn Schumann and Kirby Smart could deploy him as a Chambliss stopper. With 4.5 40-yard dash speed and nearly 34-inch arms, Cole has earned his nickname of "Tarantula." Look for the Bulldogs to spy Chambliss with him and use him as a blitzer too; he leads Georgia in pressures (24) and pass-rush win rate (17.4%). With Cole hunting Chambliss and the Bulldogs' defense ranking top 20 in rush success rate (37.8%), Ole Miss will struggle to find the end zone. The reigning SEC champion Bulldogs have one loss, but the Rebels have two and can't afford a third. What happens here will have a major effect on the shape of the College Football Playoff. Here are five trends we expect will determine who walks off the field a winner. 1. Ole Miss puts the game in Trinidad Chambliss' hands Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss has been one of the SEC's most productive offensive players, leading the conference with 2,189 passing yards and 18 touchdowns. He's also added seven rushing touchdowns. Georgia's defense allows just 14.9 points per game, ranking top 15 nationally. Expect Georgia's pass rush and secondary to credibly test Chambliss' long-range passing ambitions. His ability to extend plays and create offense with his legs could be critical. 2. Georgia establishes its running game Sep 26, 2026; Athens, Georgia, USA; Georgia Bulldogs quarterback Gunner Stockton (14) throws a pass intended for running back Chauncey Bowens (5) against the Oklahoma Sooners during the second half at Sanford Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Georgia averages 200.1 rushing yards per game, ranking third nationally. Ole Miss is one of the SEC's worst run defenses, allowing 148.9 yards on average. The Bulldogs have several capable running backs, including Dwight Phillips Jr. and Bo Walker, particularly with injuries affecting the running back rotation. If Georgia controls the line of scrimmage, it can dictate tempo, keep Chambliss on the sideline and make life difficult for the Ole Miss defense. More: Bold predictions for college football's biggest Week 10 games 3. Kewan Lacy's absence hurts Ole Miss Ole Miss running back Kewan Lacy is unlikely to play because of a shoulder injury, according to head coach Pete Golding. That puts additional pressure on Makhi Frazier and Shekai Mills-Knight to provide production. Georgia ranks second nationally in rushing defense, allowing just 86 yards per game. Without Lacy, establishing a consistent running game becomes an even bigger challenge. 4. Expect Georgia to attack early Georgia has outscored opponents 94-14 in first quarters this season. The Bulldogs have also scored 41 points per game, ranking first in the SEC. Quarterback Gunner Stockton has completed 71.8 percent of his passes. Ole Miss needs to avoid an early deficit. Georgia's ability to build leads could force the Rebels into a more predictable, pass-heavy offensive approach. 5. Ole Miss' home-field advantage matters Oct 31, 2026; Oxford, Mississippi, USA; Mississippi Rebels quarterback Trinidad Chambliss (6) looks on during the fourth quarter against the Auburn Tigers at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images The Rebels have won 16 consecutive games at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, the longest active home winning streak among Power Four programs. With the crowd behind them and a quarterback capable of creating explosive plays, Ole Miss has reasons to believe it can make this a difficult night for Georgia. The Bottom Line Georgia needs to establish its rushing attack, pressure Chambliss, and take advantage of its defensive superiority. Ole Miss needs explosive quarterback play, improved rushing production, and an early lead to build on. The biggest question: Can Ole Miss' offense generate enough against one of the nation's top-scoring defenses, particularly without its leading running back? The Big Lead prediction: Georgia 30, Ole Miss 28

away.headline: Missouri football injury updates: Official SEC report Wednesday before Georgia
away.blurb: "We were very fortunate. When you watch it, it looks bad, but the cleat was not in the ground, which is a real relief there," Mizzou head coach Eli Drinkwitz said Tuesday. "So, anticipate him trying to practice today, and we'll monitor that situation as it goes. … He was out in practice yesterday (Monday), and he is probably as tough a competitor as I've been around, so nothing would shock me more than if he wasn't playing. But, again, I don't know how his body will respond to that injury." The Tigers did, as expected, rule out defensive end Langden Kitchen, who Drinkwitz said Tuesday had surgery on his knee after sustaining an injury during the Tigers' loss to Texas this past Saturday. Kitchen will not play for Mizzou again this season. As it has since SEC play started, Mizzou ruled out running back Malae Fonoti, who is out for the season, right tackle Josh Atkins, who Eli Drinkwitz said he does not expect to be available this year, and tight end Gavin Hoffman. The possible designations, from most likely to play to least likely, are as follows: available; probable; questionable; doubtful; out. The reports are not technically injury reports, which some teams — Mizzou often included — provided in years prior. Instead, they are lists that include any players ruled unavailable or possibly unavailable for upcoming games. That could be for any number of reasons, including but not limited to injuries. away.headline: Georgia football WR Isiah Canion nowhere to be found on UGA's injury report
away.source: Dawn of the Dawg on MSN
away.blurb: Isiah Canion was one of Georgia's biggest acquisitions out of the Transfer Portal this offseason. He came to Georgia after spending two seasons at Georgia Tech, and he was expected to be a central piece of the Bulldogs' passing attack this year. He unfortunately was hurt during the second game of Georgia's season and hasn't seen the field since. Earlier this week though he was marked probable to play on Georgia's official injury report and on Thursday he was nowhere to be found on their report which means he has been officially cleared to play. This injury update does need to be taken with a grain of salt. Nate Frazier came off Georgia's injury report heading into the Alabama game, but he still didn't play. Based on that it still isn't a 100 percent guarantee that Canion will play against Ole Miss, but he most likely will be available. Chauncey Bowens still questionable to play vs Ole Miss While it looks like Georgia will finally be getting Canion back, the same can't be said for running back Chauncey Bowens. On Thursday's injury report he was still listed as questionable to play, so there is a chance he will be able to suit up against the Rebels. There however is just as good of a chance that he won't be able to play either. Another injury report will come out Friday night before one final injury update about an hour before kickoff on Saturday. Georgia's injured 3-headed monster could all return in time to play Florida Georgia WR Isiah Canion injury update is great news for UGA Canion has only recorded three receptions for 28 yards this season. That can't be held against him though because the starters barely played in Georgia's season opener against Tennessee State before he got hurt the following week in Week 2. Canion has a lot of potential though that Georgia hasn't seen yet. Last year at Georgia Tech he was an integral part of their talented offense as he recorded 33 receptions for 480 yards and four touchdowns. He isn't a player that will ever be the No. 1 target in Georgia's offense, but he can be another reliable option for Gunner Stockton in a game where UGA needs a lot of offense. This is great timing for Georgia because the Ole Miss offense, with quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, dominated UGA the two times they played last season. Georgia's offense likely needs to score a lot of points to win this game, and Canion being back on the field will help them accomplish that. Bowens hasn't played since the Vanderbilt game nearly a month ago. He is Georgia's No. 2 running back who has scored six touchdowns this season, so similarly to Canion the Bulldogs' offense would be at their best with him in the lineup against Ole Miss. Georgia thankfully has plenty of pieces in their running back room to make up for Bowens if he isn't able to play this weekend. Frazier is back for his third game since being injured and Dwight Phillips has been one of the biggest surprises so far this season, but there's no denying that Georgia would be significantly bet

away.headline: Mizzou WR Cayden Lee listed available for game against Georgia
away.blurb: Missouri wide receiver Cayden Lee was not listed on the first SEC Student-Athlete Availability Report on Wednesday. This means he is available to suit up in the contest. Lee endured a knee injury in the fourth quarter against Texas after taking a hard hit, but coach Eli Drinkwitz announced that there was no structural damage Tuesday. Drinkwitz cited the toughness of Lee in the press conference and sounded rather optimistic about his return. "He was out in practice yesterday and he is probably as tough a competitor as I've been around, so nothing would shock me more than if he wasn't playing. But again, I don't know how his body will respond to that injury," Drinkwitz said. Drinkwitz announced Tuesday that starting edge Langden Kitchen would be out for the remainder of the season. After suffering a knee injury early in the game against Texas, Kitchen had surgery Tuesday morning, per Drinkwitz. So when the injury report came out, as expected, Kitchen was listed as out. Alongside the starting edge rusher, the Tigers are without Malae Fonoti, Josh Atkins and Gavin Hoffman. The three Tigers have been out for the entirety of SEC play. Georgia has two players on the injury report: defensive tackle Josh Horton is listed as questionable for the contest. Outside linebacker Amaris Williams is also out after suffering a season-ending injury in the spring. 5 Texas starters listed as questionable ahead of contest against Mizzou football This article was originally published on www.si.com/college/missouri as Mizzou WR Cayden Lee listed available for game against Georgia . "Cayden Lee has no structural damage to the knee. We are very fortunate," Drinkwitz said. "When you watch it it looks bad, but the cleat was not in the ground, which is a real relief there, and so anticipate him trying to practice today, and we'll monitor that situation as it goes." Lee's toughness has been apparent his entire college career. Since playing 10 of 13 games his freshman year, Lee has not missed a game. He appeared in all 28 games for Ole Miss the following seasons and has played in all nine games for Missouri this year. The former third-team All-SEC selection has accumulated a career-high 62 receptions, five touchdowns and is nearing his career high in yards with a team-leading 835 yards this season. Robinson was on the preseason All-SEC First Team and has tallied 19 tackles, two interceptions and six pass deflections this season. away.headline: Terez Davis off Ole Miss injury report as Rebels prepare for Georgia
away.blurb: There weren’t many changes to the Student-Athlete Availability Report for Georgia and Ole Miss on Thursday night. The most noteworthy update was Ole Miss starting left tackle Terez Davis being removed entirely from the report . His availability for Saturday against No. 2 Georgia was never in real doubt, but we’ve seen in recent weeks players land on the report and not able to play a full game that following Saturday. Having Davis off the report means the Rebels will have its entire starting offensive line available to face a Bulldogs defense that has recorded 26 sacks this season already. And Ole Miss is going to need every bit of protection it can get. Georgia is allowing just 14.9 points and 273.4 total yards per game, ranking among the nation's best defenses in both categories. The Bulldogs have been particularly difficult to run against, surrendering just 86.8 rushing yards per game. Linebackers Chris Cole and Raylen Wilson have been especially disruptive, combining for 16.5 tackles for loss and 7.5 sacks. They're a big reason opposing offenses have struggled to consistently move the football against Georgia. That's what makes having Davis available so important. The Rebels have done an excellent job protecting quarterback Trinidad Chambliss this season, allowing just one sack over their last three games. Even when Davis missed the Texas game, Ole Miss managed to keep Chambliss upright. But Georgia presents a different challenge. With Kewan Lacy already ruled out, the Rebels will need their offensive line to create running lanes for Shekai Mills-Knight and the other running backs while also giving Chambliss enough time to find open receivers. Davis' return to the lineup against Auburn was encouraging. Having him completely off the injury report heading into one of the biggest games of the season is even better news. Offensive lineman Patrick Kutas and linebacker Keaton Thomas are among those out. Defensive end Kam Franklin and safety Sharif Denson are questionable on the initial report, released at 7:10 p.m. CT on Wednesday. Safety MJ Preston is doubtful. Quarterback Trinidad Chambliss , wide receiver Deuce Alexander and defensive tackle Will Echoles are listed as probable. Ole Miss (6-3, 4-3 SEC) and Oklahoma (5-4, 3-3 SEC) kick off at 3:15 p.m. CT Saturday on SEC Network. Five safeties are on the Ole Miss report. Edwin Joseph, Gerald Lacy Jr. and Nascar McCoy are out, MJ Preston is doubtful and Sharif Denson is questionable. Preston was listed as probable on last week’s initial report, and Denson was not listed at all. Joseph has been out with an injury for about a month. Safety Joenel Aguero said Tuesday that cornerback Jaylon Braxton has helped fill that gap by moving around in the secondary. Aguero and Braxton are not on the report. Kutas out on the offensive line Kutas was the only player Golding said Monday the Rebels knew for sure would be unavailable. Carius Curne is also out, as he was on last week’s initial report. Terez Davis, who was probable last week, is not on this report. Thomas was questionable on last week’s initial report and probable by Friday. He is now out, along with Ant Davis Jr. and JaMichael Garrett, who is new to the out list. Suntarine Perkins and Luke Ferrelli are not on the report. Running back Kewan Lacy remains out. Golding was asked Monday whether he would be available this week and said, “No, he will not be playing this week.” Alexander is listed as probable after Golding said he was banged up late in the loss to Georgia. “He should be fine for this week,” Golding said. “We’ll manage this week.” Wide receivers Izaiah Hartrup and Kervin Johnson Jr. are both out. Chambliss and Echoles are also probable. Oklahoma lists five players out, one doubtful and four questionable. The offensive line is the biggest concern for the Sooners. Fred Hinton is out, Ryan Fodje is doubtful and Caleb Nitta is questionable, while Eddy Pierre-Louis is probable. Linebacker Taylor Heim is out, and linebackers Cole Sullivan and James Nesta are questionable. Running back Tory Blaylock is questionable, and wide receiver Trell Harris and tight end Trynae Washington are out. home.headline: Kewan Lacy injury update, latest news on star Ole Miss RB for Oklahoma game
home.blurb: OXFORD — Ole Miss football running back Kewan Lacy is out for the Rebels' game against Oklahoma. Lacy has been out for the last two Ole Miss games after being hurt against Texas on Oct. 24. He dislocated his left shoulder against the Longhorns . It's the same shoulder that he had offseason surgery on before the season. Golding also said guard Patrick Kutas is out for the game against the Sooners after being injured against Georgia. Ole Miss is expecting to have receiver Deuce Alexander available. Alexander exited late in the game against Georgia, but walked off the field under his own power. No. 17 Ole Miss (6-3, 4-3 SEC) will play at Oklahoma (5-4, 3-3) on Nov. 14 (3:15 p.m., SEC Network). Ole Miss coach Pete Golding confirmed Lacy's status on Nov. 9 at his weekly press conference. The Ole Miss rushing offense was not effective against Georgia without Lacy. The Rebels rushed 31 times for 66 yards against the Bulldogs on Nov. 7 in a 42-7 loss. Lacy has 78 rushes for 391 yards and five touchdowns in 2026. Injuries have hampered his stats compared to 2025. He has missed three complete games. Lacy rushed for 1,567 yards and a school-record 24 touchdowns in 2025. Who is Ole Miss football RB behind Kewan Lacy? Makhi Frazier and Shekai Mills-Knight have emerged as the primary running backs behind Lacy. Frazier is second on the team with 72 rushes. He has 365 yards. Mills-Knight has earned an increased workload as the season has gone along. He has 33 carries for 165 yards and three touchdowns. Sam Hutchens covers Ole Miss for the Clarion Ledger. home.headline: Ole Miss Suffers Another Major Injury Blow as Patrick Kutas Joins Kewan Lacy
home.blurb: Golding also noted on Monday that standout right guard Patrick Kutas won’t be available to play in Saturday’s Week 11 matchup between the Rebels and Sooners. Ole Miss’ first-year head coach mentioned Deuce Alexander got nicked up against Georgia as well, but isn’t expected to miss time. “Not (any) season-ending (injuries). Kutas got banged up pretty good, so we will not have Patrick this week,” Golding explained. “There will be some moving parts to that and looking at some guys bumping inside and we’ve been rotating some guys anyway. But he’s the only one (besides Kewan Lacy) that we know for sure won’t be available on Saturday.” During the first half of Ole Miss’ 35-point loss to Georgia, Kutas got rolled up on in a pile of players on a run play. Kutas walked off the field with assistance and was later able to pedal on the exercise bike along the Rebels’ sideline, but did not return to the game at any point. With Three Losses, Ole Miss’ CFP Hopes Feel out of Reach OXFORD, Miss. — Star Ole Miss running back Kewan Lacy is set to miss his third straight game when the Rebels travel to Norman, Oklahoma this weekend, according to head coach Pete Golding. It will mark Lacy's fourth missed game of the year , but he won’t be alone. For his efforts against Missouri and Auburn, the Southeastern Conference named Kutas the SEC Offensive Lineman of the Week twice within three weeks. Kutas’ absence will be a big blow for an Ole Miss offense that is set to visit one of the country’s best defensive fronts. The Sooners allow an average of 122.7 rushing yards per game, good for 36th-best in the country, and are up to 26 total sacks this season. Among the weaknesses for Ole Miss against Georgia was its ability to maintain a stable front for Trinidad Chambliss and the run game. According to ESPN Insights, Chambliss faced pressure on 33 percent of dropbacks (season-high) completing just two-of-eight passes for 13 yards and an interception (four sacks) in Week 10. “We just couldn’t get things going. Couldn’t get drives going,” Chambliss said of the Rebels’ offensive struggles. “They brought a lot of pressure, they got home on four sacks. We just couldn’t get going. I mean, they just brought a lot at us, so it’s tough to kind of get into a flow of that when you’re getting pressured and extending plays — or trying to at least.” Oklahoma will more than likely attempt to replicate that winning formula on the defensive side of the ball. Ole Miss is trying to bounce-back into the win column to help salvage any good feelings about the 2026 season. “Obviously there’s a feeling of disappointment, regardless of how many it is,” Golding said of the team mood following its third loss. “They put a lot into this and they want to put their focus on their preparation and playing well — and we didn’t play well. We didn’t coach well, we didn’t play well and that’s the outcome you’re going to get when you do that. But I think they did a really good job last night of focusing on the why

Pete Fiutak · College Football News Sat, November 7, 2026 at 2:18 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads When we last saw Oklahoma and Florida play, the Sooners rolled 55-20 in the 2020 Cotton Bowl over a high-powered Gator team that lost to eventual national champion Alabama in an epic SEC Championship. The other meeting was the BCS Championship at the end of the 2009 season, when Tim Tebow and the Gator defense took down Heisman-winner Sam Bradford and the amazing Sooner attack 24-14 for the national title. The stakes aren't as high this time around, but for a Florida program that's on the rise, and No. 24 in the first College Football Playoff rankings, and for a 4-4 Oklahoma desperate to close strong, this will be intense. Oklahoma vs Florida: Quick Hits Oklahoma at 4-4, needs to win two of its last four to be bowl eligible. It hosts Ole Miss and Texas A&M after this before closing at Missouri. Florida is coming off the 27-8 loss to Georgia. It goes to Kentucky next, hosts Vanderbilt, and finishes at Florida State. Again, the first two meetings were in big bowl games. This is the first regular season matchup between the two. How To Watch Oklahoma vs Florida Date: Saturday, November 7, 2026 Game Time: 7:45 PM ET TV: SEC Network Location: Ben Hill Griffin Stadium, Gainesville, FL – Week 10 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Expert Picks: Week 10 Why Oklahoma Will Win The defense continues to fight the good fight. It had a problem in the 42-25 loss to South Carolina, but the defense is fantastic on third downs thanks to a pass rush that takes over games. But to beat Florida, you have to slow down the run. The Gators are 0-3 when running for fewer than 155 yards, and the Sooners give up just 107 yards per game. Only Mississippi State and, last week, South Carolina have been able to gash the Sooners for more. Why Florida Will Win Oklahoma's offense has a hard time running the ball. With a defense as good as the Sooners have, all the O has to do is keep it moving and not screw it up. But no running game means more pressing overall, and then come the mistakes. The Sooners only average 107 yards per game on the ground, and they just can't find any room to move. The Gators have to hold up, and then pounce on an Oklahoma attack that turned it over four times against both Georgia and Kentucky, three times against New Mexico, and twice against Michigan. Oklahoma vs Florida Prediction, Betting Lines It's stupid, but if you buy into these things, going back to the last two games of last season, Oklahoma is on a ten-game run of alternating wins and losses. The Sooners beat Texas, then lost to Kentucky, beat Mississippi State, lost to South Carolina, beat … Florida? The Sooners have the defense to hold up and make Florida struggle. The Gators got by Texas a few weeks ago, but it's been a struggle, losing three of the last four. Weird trends aside, this Oklahoma team really does have a way of rallying when it absolutely has to. The Sooners need to win two of their final four to earn bowl eligibility . With a new voice leading the offense, the Sooners are hoping for a turnaround to end the 2026 season. Jason Witten takes over an offense that has underachieved this season, given the number of returning starters along the offensive line and the weapons at returning quarterback John Mateer. How much better can Oklahoma be in a week is the question on everyone's minds. It's unlikely the Sooners will suddenly erupt on offense, but if they find more consistency, they'll have a chance to finish the season on a high note. So how will the Sooners perform in "The Swamp?" Our staff here at Sooners Wire picked this week's showdown between the Sooners and the Gators. Too Many Questions Oklahoma tight ends coach Jason Witten, left, talks with coach Brent Venables during a Sooners football spring practice in Norman, Okla., Thursday, April 9, 2026. There are just too many moving parts for Oklahoma to reliably believe the Sooners could win a road game in the swamp. The Sooners have made a change at offensive coordinator and the availability of a bunch of notable players on both sides of the ball are still in question. There's also the question of how Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer will play without Ben Arbuckle on the sideline for the first time in years. Even though Florida has a few issues to worry about as well, they're certainly not as dire as Oklahoma's at the moment. Florida 21, Oklahoma 10 James D. Jackson, Contributor Improved Sooners Touchdowns? Touchdowns. Oklahoma made a huge move this week by letting go of Ben Arbuckle and having Jason Witten call plays. Witten called plays as a high school head coach and had a ton of success doing it. I think the offense will play with a fire we haven't seen this year, and the defense will return to its dominant ways. Because of that, I've got OU winning and the offense scoring three touchdowns. For now, though, the only change is the absence of OC Ben Arbuckle, so all of Oklahoma's other offensive problems remain. Expect OU's defense to bounce back against Florida, but expect the offense to continue faltering for the remainder of this season. Florida 16, Oklahoma 7 Aaron Gelvin, Contributor Promising, but Sooners struggle Oct 31, 2026; Norman, Oklahoma, USA; Oklahoma Sooners quarterback John Mateer (10) throws during the first quarter against the South Carolina Gamecocks at Gaylord Family-Oklahoma Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images As much as I'd like to believe that things are going to magically turn around, it's hard to create that expectation. Jason Witten may be the answer to what ails John Mateer and the Oklahoma Sooners offense. However, until we see it, there's no telling what you'll get from Witten's crew. Expect the defense to bounce back and play well against Jaden Baugh and the Gators' rushing attack, but with injury concerns in the secondary, the Sooners may have a hard time slowing down Tramell Jones. picks.headline: Staff Picks: Will Oklahoma Get Back on Track at No. 24 Florida?
picks.blurb: Staff Picks: Will Oklahoma Get Back on Track at No. 24 Florida? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NFL news, live updates Misiorowski, Schlittler win Cy Youngs NFL midseason awards Rex Ryan arrested Skubal suitors emerge Staff Picks: Will Oklahoma Get Back on Track at No. 24 Florida? Oklahoma Sooners tight ends coach Jason Witten will take over as interim offensive coordinator for the rest of the season. | Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Ryan Chapman · Oklahoma Sooners On SI Fri, November 6, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Gators have an impressive resume, having beaten No. 4 Ole Miss 52-28 at The Swamp, then going on the road to Austin and taking down No. 7 Texas 27-24 - one week after OU beat them in Dallas - on a night the underwhelming Florida defense overwhelmed Arch Manning and the Longhorns, sacking him five times, limiting UT to 2-of-10 on third down (they had 13 first downs total) and holding the Horns to 272 total yards. But they were also blown out in back-to-back losses to No. 25 Missouri and unranked South Carolina, which preceded last week's 27-8 loss to No. 3 Georgia. Oklahoma is a touchdown underdog to Florida, but the Sooners are the best defense the Gators face. Still, OU may be reeling after its worst defensive performance in years in the blowout loss to South Carolina - which included an incomprehensible 25 missed tackles (usually 10 is a bad number). OU's first trip to The Swamp will be punctuated by another big game from Gators RB Jaden Baugh, who's third in the SEC at 100.3 rushing yards per game and first with 13 rushing TDs. Final score: Florida 28, Oklahoma 21 Things could get gross Saturday night. Florida has officially made a quarterback change, and Tramell Jones Jr. could be without a pair of key weapons to pair with an already banged up offensive line. Oklahoma's offense has been so bad it got its coordinator fired, but Jason Witten has never called plays collegiately and John Mateer is still likely the quarterback the Sooners will roll with. OU's defense needs to bounce back after its tackling struggles last week, but even an improved showing could see Gator running back Jaden Baugh have enough success to push Jon Sumrall's team across the finish line. Final: Florida 16, Oklahoma 13 OU is set up for further disaster as it heads to the swamp. Jason Witten will serve as the Sooners' play caller for the first time at the college level, John Mateer is still the quarterback and Ben Hill Griffin Stadium is one of the nation's most hostile atmospheres. But amid the weirdness, I expect OU to win this game. Teams often come out more inspired after a notable firing, and I predict Witten will lead a creative game plan as he auditions for the full-time offensive coordinator role. Florida's offense is good - but it is also prone to turning the ball over. If the Sooners are able to put pressure on Tramell Jones Jr. early, it will create a long day for the Gators' offense. Final: Oklahoma 24, Florida 20 The Sooners figure to get a little boost from Jason Witten's playcalling, but don't expect massive changes in either scheme or production here. The offensive line still has its issues, John Mateer hasn't been consistent at all, and neither of the other quarterbacks have experience in games like this. But Oklahoma's defense does figure to have a bounce-back game after struggling to contain LaNorris Sellers and the South Carolina offense. The tackling will be better, and Florida's offense is in a bit of flux itself with Tramell Jones Jr. expected to make his second start of the season at quarterback and Florida's offensive line struggling in recent weeks. But the Gators still have plenty of talent, especially on the offensive side, and The Swamp is one of the toughest environments in college football. That's a tough position for a reeling team to be placed in. The game will be close into the second half but the Gators figure to pull away and hand Oklahoma its second consecutive defeat. Final: Florida 24, Oklahoma 14 Brady Trantham A new offensive coordinator doesn'tchange the fact that John Mateer is still QB1 at OU. Mateer gives Oklahoma their best shot in any game, but in 20 games as the Sooner signal caller, it is apparent that he simply isn't very good. A coaching change can, in theory, help him in spots, but if OU needs their QB to make a play in a tight game, chances are he will make that play - just for the other team. Florida sticks to the run and gets Oklahoma on a few explosives and rides it to an easy win. Offensive lineman Patrick Kutas and linebacker Keaton Thomas are among those out. Defensive end Kam Franklin and safety Sharif Denson are questionable on the initial report, released at 7:10 p.m. CT on Wednesday. Safety MJ Preston is doubtful. Quarterback Trinidad Chambliss , wide receiver Deuce Alexander and defensive tackle Will Echoles are listed as probable. Ole Miss (6-3, 4-3 SEC) and Oklahoma (5-4, 3-3 SEC) kick off at 3:15 p.m. CT Saturday on SEC Network. Five safeties are on the Ole Miss report. Edwin Joseph, Gerald Lacy Jr. and Nascar McCoy are out, MJ Preston is doubtful and Sharif Denson is questionable. Preston was listed as probable on last week’s initial report, and Denson was not listed at all. Joseph has been out with an injury for about a month. Safety Joenel Aguero said Tuesday that cornerback Jaylon Braxton has helped fill that gap by moving around in the secondary. Aguero and Braxton are not on the report. Kutas out on the offensive line Kutas was the only player Golding said Monday the Rebels knew for sure would be unavailable. Carius Curne is also out, as he was on last week’s initial report. Terez Davis, who was probable last week, is not on this report. Thomas was questionable on last week’s initial report and probable by Friday. He is now out, along with Ant Davis Jr. and JaMichael Garrett, who is new to the out list. Suntarine Perkins and Luke Ferrelli are not on the report. Running back Kewan Lacy remains out. Chambliss and Echoles are also probable. Oklahoma lists five players out, one doubtful and four questionable. The offensive line is the biggest concern for the Sooners. Fred Hinton is out, Ryan Fodje is doubtful and Caleb Nitta is questionable, while Eddy Pierre-Louis is probable. Linebacker Taylor Heim is out, and linebackers Cole Sullivan and James Nesta are questionable. Running back Tory Blaylock is questionable, and wide receiver Trell Harris and tight end Trynae Washington are out. Ole Miss coach Pete Golding confirmed his squad will be without two of its most important offensive players when the Rebels line up against the Sooners. Golding said running back Kewan Lacy and starting offensive lineman Patrick Kutas will miss the game. So far this season, the Sooners have typically had the least desirable injury report. But the two losses for Ole Miss are fairly significant, especially given the Rebels are coming off their third loss of the season. Golding said Kutas was injured in Ole Miss’ 42-7 loss at Georgia on Nov. 7. The Rebels will have to make adjustments across the offensive line. Former Sooner Troy Everett will likely replace Kutas at right guard as he did against Georgia. “Not season-ending,” Golding said of Kutas’ injury in his weekly presser. “Kutas got banged up pretty good, so we will not have Patrick this week. So there will be some moving parts to that and looking at some guys bumping inside. Golding later clarified Lacy will not play either. Against the Sooners last season, Lacy rushed 27 times for 78 yards and two touchdowns to help No. 8 Ole Miss defeat No. 13 Oklahoma 34–26. This season, however, he has missed a handful of games due to injury. Lacy missed the Georgia game, and it was a noticeable absence. Ole Miss (6-3, 4-3 SEC) mustered only 7 points against the Bulldogs. Lacy was a Doak Walker Award finalist last season. The honor is presented annually to the nation's top college football running back. He has run for five touchdowns this season but hasn’t seen the field since dislocating his shoulder against Texas in October. Ole Miss has lost two of the last three games in his absence. Oklahoma (5-4, 3-3 SEC) will have an opportunity to take advantage in Norman with kickoff scheduled for 3:15 p.m. CT. The game will be televised on the SEC Network. This is the third straight season the Sooners have played the Rebels and second straight season Oklahoma has hosted them. The league named the two schools annual rivals last season, meaning they'll play each other at home every season for at least the next four years. Ole Miss is 3-0 against the Sooners, who are trying to build on a 23-7 win over Florida . A win would also keep Oklahoma's bowl streak alive. The Sooners also got good news on the defensive side of the ball, with cornerback Eli Bowen set to return after missing the last four games. S Peyton Bowen: GAME-TIME DECISION Safety Peyton Bowen was also listed on the injury report last week before ultimately being available against South Carolina. Hopefully, it's the same conclusion this week but he's even healthier, because Bowen is a vital piece of OU's defense as one of 15 semifinalists for the Jim Thorpe Award, which goes to the best defensive back in college football. Replacement: If Bowen can't go, Michael Boganowski should get the start after also starting last week, even with Bowen available. Florida's QB play won't be as good, but Boganowski made some early mistakes against South Carolina, so the Sooners need Bowen out there. OL Eddy Pierre-Louis: GAME-TIME DECISION Offensive lineman Eddy Pierre-Louis hasn't seen the field since Week 4 against Georgia because of an injury. It looks like he will miss another one on Saturday, meaning he's officially been out more games than he's played this season after starting at guard the first three weeks. Wide receiver Elijah Thomas, who was listed as probable on Friday, will make his return after missing the past two games. He's caught five passes for 49 yards this season. ILB Jaden Robinson: out OL Emeka Ugorji: out TE Evan Chieca: out DL Jeramiah McCloud: out WR Vernell Brown III: out It's been a week of change for the Oklahoma Sooners, including players actually getting healthier instead of getting worse on the availability report. Newly appointed interim offensive coordinator Jason Witten will get the rare occurrence in Norman of having nearly his entire starting offensive line healthy for his play-calling debut against No. 24 Florida on Saturday night. S Peyton Bowen: GAME-TIME DECISION Safety Peyton Bowen was also listed on the injury report last week before ultimately being available against South Carolina. Hopefully, it's the same conclusion this week but he's even healthier, because Bowen is a vital piece of OU's defense as one of 15 semifinalists for the Jim Thorpe Award, which goes to the best defensive back in college football. Replacement: If Bowen can't go, Michael Boganowski should get the start after also starting last week, even with Bowen available. Florida's QB play won't be as good, but Boganowski made some early mistakes against South Carolina, so the Sooners need Bowen out there. OL Eddy Pierre-Louis: GAME-TIME DECISION Offensive lineman Eddy Pierre-Louis hasn't seen the field since Week 4 against Georgia because of an injury. It looks like he will miss another one on Saturday, meaning he's officially been out more games than he's played this season after starting at guard the first three weeks. Wide receiver Elijah Thomas, who was listed as probable on Friday, will make his return after missing the past two games. He's caught five passes for 49 yards this season. ILB Jaden Robinson: out OL Emeka Ugorji: out TE Evan Chieca: out DL Jeramiah McCloud: out WR Vernell Brown III: out It's been a week of change for the Oklahoma Sooners, including players actually getting healthier instead of getting worse on the availability report. Newly appointed interim offensive coordinator Jason Witten will get the rare occurrence in Norman of having nearly his entire starting offensive line healthy for his play-calling debut against No. 24 Florida on Saturday night. That alone should have OU's offense looking better after Ben Arbuckle was fired on Monday. OU, though, can still never go a week without a lengthy injured list. Brown will miss his fifth straight game with a grade-1 PCL strain that he suffered against Ole Miss in Week 4; it was re-aggravated ahead of last week's Georgia game. "So he was not available at practice today," Jon Sumrall said on Monday . "I really don't have a really strong feeling on timeline because everything early in the week last week was trending really positively until the setback on Wednesday. It sucks. It sucks for him. He's working like hell to try to get back. He's frustrated." The four others listed as out for the showdown in the Swamp are defensive lineman Jeramiah McCloud, tight end Evan Chieca, offensive lineman Emeka Ugorji and linebacker Jaden Robinson. McCloud is out due to a suspension, according to Swamp247 , while Robinson missed his first game of the season last week against Georgia. The good news is that the other two on the availability report — wide receiver Bailey Stockton and defensive lineman Emmanuel Oyebadejo — have been upgraded from questionable to probable. Both players were initially listed as doubtful last week; they ended up playing against Georgia. Offensive lineman Eddy Pierre-Louis remains listed as doubtful, while defensive back Peyton Bowen is listed as questionable; wide receiver Elijah Thomas and defensive lineman Kenny Ozowalu are listed as probable. Wide receiver Jer'Michael Carter, defensive back Eli Bowen, tight end Rocky Beers and offensive lineman Jake Maikkula are now cleared to play.
